articleTitle: Virtual Inertia Support in AGC of Deregulated Interconnected Power System with Penetration of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This article proposes a virtual inertia control based Electric Vehicle (EV) structure to enhance Power System Frequency Regulation (FR). Modern networks have significantly less inertia than older ones, therefore keeping reserves of power (like batteries) would need very fast regulatory responses to reduce frequency swings in the grid. The power system under study incorporates many real-time nonlinearities, such as boiler dynamics, generation rate constraint (GRC), and governor dead band (GDB), in addition to three distinct energy sources-gas, hydro, and thermal-in each control region. Three controllers-TID, ID- T, and PID- T (proposed)-are applicable to both scheduled and unscheduled power under various contracts, including poolco, bilateral, and contract violation-based transactions, using different tie-lines. A new type of modified Proportional-Integral-Derivative- Tilt (PID- T) controller has been created and compared with a few controllers that are currently in use. To optimize the several parameters of the suggested controller, a modified version of the Sea-horse Optimisation (SHO) approach has been used. A few well-known meta-heuristic algorithms are compared to the SHO in order to show its superiority. Under bilateral-based transactions, analysis was conducted to verify the robustness and flexibility of the suggested controller. The extensive research results provide compelling evidence supporting the value and effectiveness of the suggested controller and optimization.

articleTitle: Combined PCA and Kernel-Based Extreme Learning Machine Technique for Classification of Faults in IEEE 9- Bus System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Knowledge of system parameters and faults is one of the utmost needs to minimize supply interruption. In the interconnected grid, the stability and reliability of the supply are guaranteed with a dedicated protection scheme to reduce the time of system disruptions caused by faults. This work proposes a fault identification and classification scheme constructed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) as a signal processing technique and Kernel-based Extreme Learning Machine (KELM) as a robust classifier tool. An IEEE-9 Bus system consisting of loads, buses, transformers, and generators is considered for the fault assessment. The PSCAD/EMTDC software is used to simulate the power system, and an algorithm has been developed using MATLAB code. PCA is employed to collect the useful features from acquired current signals of the line. These features are later migrated to the KELM for fault data classification. The faulty line identification and fault type classification accuracy of the proposed technique are 100% and 99.91 % respectively. Moreover, the proposed technique is effective considering the variation in fault types, fault impedance, fault inception angle, fault location, and loading effect.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Fault Prediction in MetroPT Datasets: Enhanced Diagnosis and Efficient Failure Prediction through Innovative Data Refinement
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This scientific paper presents groundbreaking advancements in Predictive Maintenance (PdM) within Industry 4.0, employing cutting-edge machine learning classification algorithms for fault prediction and diagnosis in Air Production Unit (APU) systems like MetroPT and MetroPT -3. This research uses data-driven methodologies to optimize feature extraction techniques to enhance fault prediction and improve diagnostic accuracy. A robust and versatile model emerges through comprehensive testing, displaying exceptional potential in fault prediction and diagnosis for complex systems. The paper highlights the significance of enhanced analytical techniques, such as cross-validation, ensuring the reliability and robustness of the model, contributing to refined and accurate fault prediction and diagnosis, all without succumbing to overfitting. This work significantly advances the application of machine learning in predicting malignancy within Industry 4.0, showcasing the promise of these methodologies in fault prediction and diagnosis for intricate systems.

articleTitle: A New Common Ground Single-Phase Transformerless Five-Level Inverter for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The paper presents a new common ground single-phase transformerless five-level inverter for Photovoltaic (PV) applications. The topology is built with a minimum of six switches and three capacitors compared to various five-level inverter proposed in the literature and has the advantage of 100% dc-link utilization. The topology has the capability to supply both real power and reactive power. In order to achieve this, a simple level-shifted pulse width modulation scheme is used and proportional-resonant (PR) controller is developed to study the dynamic response of the system under input voltage as well as grid current changes. The performance of the proposed topology and their control scheme is validated through MATLAB simulation results. Finally, a detailed comparison is made with the recent five-level inverter topologies to highlight the merits of the proposed topolozy.

articleTitle: Power Factor Correction by Phase Angle Regulation using Multi Level Inverter based DVR
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper focused on power factor improvement in distribution system along with sag, swell mitigation using dynamic voltage restorer (DVR). The DVR model employs a 5-level transistor clamped H-Bridge (TCHB) inverter. A new control scheme is designed for the DVR to enhance the source side power factor while simultaneously compensating voltage sag and voltage swell. The proposed technique is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink for different conditions, power factor improvement with sag, power factor improvement without sag and sag/swell mitigation. It is observed that the proposed controller is working satisfactorily for enhancing power factor with voltage sag & swell mitigation in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Tracking Using Machine Learning Technique in Hybrid Solar-Wind Renewable Energy Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Hybrid renewable energy sources (HRES), particularly solar and wind, have gained interest and grown rapidly to address the energy crisis. At the same time, the problem arose due to the nonlinearity of the sources over time. Regardless of the environmental conditions, HRES can operate at the maximum power point using Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technology. Due to the economic advantages, several controllers are being developed to maximize the performance of the HRES. The traditional controllers had limitations: slower response speed and different step sizes. To ensure the maximum availability of power from the HRES under varying system conditions, the hybrid Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) controller with Walrus Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is proposed in this work. The proposed WOA hybrid GBDT (WOHGD) studies the optimal duty cycle of the boost converter in a solar wind connected power system. The proposed work is implemented on the MATLAB/SIMULINK tool, and the results are verified with existing approaches.

articleTitle: Utilization of Road Infrastructure with a Hybrid of Solar PV and SEGP Energy for Drinking Water and eBike Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Freshwater scarcity and the increasing energy crisis are major issues worldwide. Clean water, essential to human civilization, is in growing demand, requiring sustainable management that requires energy. Simultaneously, the energy crisis escalates due to depleting fossil fuel reserves and increasing carbon footprint-related climatic issues, thus necessitating a shift to sustainable energy sources. The transportation sector is also transitioning from fuel-based to electric vehicles, increasing the demand for electrical energy. This research proposes a pioneering hybrid solution. In response to these formidable challenges, an innovative hybrid energy and freshwater generation system is developed using solar PV and Sustainable Energy Generating Pad (SEGP) technology integrated into road infrastructure. Thus, a combined station is established and embedded within the road pavement. This multifunctional station serves as a charging hub for electric bikes and mobile devices while simultaneously generating freshwater, contributing to alleviating water and energy scarcity. This integrated hybrid energy solution holds the potential to be a game-changer, addressing the pressing concerns of water and energy scarcity while actively contributing to global sustainability endeavors. Its innovative approach and multifaceted utility offer a promising pathway toward a greener and more sustainable world.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Lithium-Ion Battery Storage System on Sustainable Energy-Generating Pad Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The generation of electricity from Renewable Energy (RE) sources is the best alternative worldwide because of the current geopolitical and environmental situations. An efficient energy storage system is vital to making a sustainable RE system. The standard electrical energy storage devices are Nickel, Lead-acid batteries, Supercapacitors, and Lithium-ion Batteries. However, energy storage in lithium-ion batteries is the best choice today because of their long lifetime, high energy density, and low energy loss at shelf-discharging. In this research, A Sustainable Energy Generating Pad (SEGP) for bike lane applications has been developed and prototyped in the SMART Center at PV AMU. Impact energy from running bikes on SEGP was stored by a lab developed novel Dual-Stage Charging System (DSCS) using 18650 lithium-ion batteries. In the lab experiments, from a 3-foot-long SEGP, energy stored in a lithium-ion battery in the first stage of the DSCS was around 11 mWh/cell. The maximum Voltage reached around 4.2 V. Finally, the results tested were compared and verified. The results were similar by approximately 97%, corresponding to two case studies by well-known companies such as Toshiba and Samsung.

articleTitle: Identification of Erroneous Line Parameter in Three-Phase Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Accurate knowledge of line parameters is quintessential for distribution system operators (DSO) as it significantly influences energy management planning. This paper presents an identification method for erroneous line parameters using the Normalized Lagrange Multiplier test (NLM) and line parameter estimation on the three-phase distribution system. The presented method is further tested and validated on the IEEE 123 bus distribution test system.

articleTitle: Health Monitoring of Solar Photovoltaic Panels and Data Acquisition System using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: With depleting non-renewable resources and concern for global warming, efforts are being made to shift to renewable energy sources. Renewable energy resources are freely available into the nature. The efforts are made to convert these resources into electrical energy and use them to fulfil the energy needs, but they face operational challenges and require constant technological innovation. At present, most of the energy produced by renewable sources comes from solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Monitoring all those PV systems, especially remote ones, is a tough task. Thus, this work is aimed to contribute to develop solar PV health monitoring and data acquisition system using internet of things (IoT) technology. In this paper, there is a provision of monitoring and logging multiple parameters like current, voltage, power, ambient temperature, panel temperature, humidity, solar irradiance etc. of a solar PV system in the real time. Anyone with correct authorization can access the live data feed and visualize all the previous data with the help of multiple plots. To achieve this, the solar PV module is operated in multiple conditions and all the corresponding data are logged and live monitored. The solar PV health monitoring system makes system much more robust and ready to be used in industries.

articleTitle: Investigating Neural Network Hyperparameter Variations in Robotic Arm Inverse Kinematics for Different Arm Lengths
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This research delves into the evaluation of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) in tackling the intricate domain of inverse kinematics problems within the context of robotic systems. Compared to direct kinematics, inverse kinematics presents significant challenges, especially when dealing with different arm lengths, which can impact the system's overall functionality. In this study, we conduct a comprehensive comparative analysis to assess the performance of ANNs across various robotic arm lengths. Following the forward kinematics of a simple 2-DoF robotic manipulator, three distinct datasets (fixed step size, random step size, and sinusoidal step size) are generated for training, testing, and validation phases. For every dataset, three optimizers, namely Levenberg Marquardt, Bayesian Regularization, and Scaled Conjugate Gradient, are considered with different hyperparameters to investigate the performance of the ANN models. Based on the validation of MSE values, ANN models with different hyperparameters are found to be a promising approach in estimating the inverse kinematic solutions for different arm lengths with data complexities. Such solutions can be further extended to higher DoF robotic solutions and save the computational burden of evaluating analytical solutions.

articleTitle: Real-time Solar Power Optimization and Energy Monitoring System with Maximum Power Point Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The increasing global demand for electricity underscores the need to transition from fossil fuels to sustainable alternatives like solar energy. Despite solar power's advantages of abundance, sustainability, and quiet operation, environmental factors such as temperature and irradiance affect the efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) systems. This study utilizes the Perturb and Observe (P&O) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) approach to optimize a PV panel, validated through a cost-effective Arduino-based hardware model. The approach integrates simulation and practical testing, offering insights into energy production variations under diverse conditions, with parameters continuously monitored and updated on a web server.

articleTitle: Lemurs Algorithm for Optimal Location and Sizing of Distributed Generation in Electrical Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Demand for electricity has been steadily increasing recently. Because of this, it is important to not only use all the new energy sources that are available to make electricity, but also to lower power loss in the distribution system to an acceptable limit. This paper aims to lessen the real power loss in the distribution network. Distributed generation (DG) units can help meet energy needs and improve efficiency of the electrical supply system. To reduce power loss, it is important to figure out placement and size DG units that use green energy sources. This paper shows the Lemurs Optimizer algorithm to evaluate size and placement of DG units. The real power loss is reduced by 90.9%, 34.5% and 65.9% for type-III, type-II and type-I DG, respectively. The results show that DG penetration helps reach the suggested goal. The findings show that the LO is more effective and reliable for improving the performance of the distribution network. The method is tested on IEEE 33 bus radial distribution test system.

articleTitle: Optimal Selection of Evolutionary Based MPPT Algorithm for PV Arrays Under Multiple Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Considering significant interest in clean energy in recent times, integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems has become in widespread. PV systems operating under partial shading conditions (PSCs) influences its profitability. Under PSC, PV system exhibit multiple local maximum power points (LMPPs) and one global maximum power point (GMPP). This work aims to study the performance and comparative analysis of 4 popular metaheuristic MPP algorithms under multiple partial shading conditions. The techniques studied are Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA), Cuckoo Search Optimization Algorithm (CSO), Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm (GWO), and Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm (PSO). The tracking performance is evaluated under fast changing 5 shading scenarios. Results show that all the metaheuristic algorithms are found to have fast response and able to converge to their final steady state value within a short time of nearly 0.1s. However, for diverse shading scenarios, different algorithms are found to perform better. Thus a unique metaheuristic algorithm is not optimal for all shading scenarios. The energy yield calculations is proposed as a basis for optimal algorithm selection. GWO is identified as the optimal algorithm with the best energy output when shading scenarios have equal duration.

articleTitle: Blockchain based Enhanced Healthcare Framework for Secure Interoperability
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Medical history of patients is sensitive and crucial for the treatment. During epidemics like COVID-19, secure data exchange between hospitals is very important. However, shareability of data with security in existing healthcare system is a big concern. To overcome this, we have presented a blockchain based enhanced healthcare system for secure interoperability. To protect the system from external threats, hospitals are connected to each other with the distributed networks. And to protect the system from internal threats, a hospital is further divided into distributed peers where a peer represents a section or a department of hospital. Identity managers are implemented at both peer and organizational levels to ensure efficient access control. Through simulation analysis, we have found that the reading and writing throughput is improved around 16 % and 25 % with respect to existing method.

articleTitle: Robust and Explainable AI: Auto-Augment with Label Preservation and Saliency Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) relies on models that are reliable and simple to comprehend. Generative AI is a subset of AI as it can generate something new and unique from random noise or existing data inputs regarding an image, text, and data. In auto-augmentation, a generative AI can help developers better plan and estimate work. This research covers two critical areas of AI research: auto-augmentation and explainability. Additionally, our approach makes machine learning models more accessible to read by maintaining the purity of labels and adding saliency factors for better performance. The data is changed using auto-augmentation methods to improve model adaptation during training. These changes could alter ground truth labels, impacting how well the model works. We offer a label preservation way to rectify issues, ensuring data enhancement processes maintain label consistency. Applying the suggested method's saliency parameters makes it easier to understand how the model's forecasts work, which increases their dependability and openness. Using intermediate layer models without knowing anything about the domain makes hard-positive cases that keep the original labels. It improves performance across disciplines. Seeking model explainability is done with parameter saliency maps. It makes it easier to understand how models behave by finding and studying the network factors that lead to bad decisions. Using a ResNet18 classifier, the suggested method is tested thoroughly on the CIFAR100 dataset.

articleTitle: Real-Time SOC Estimation of Li-ion Battery Pack Using Improved Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A battery Management System (BMS) is an electronic system that enables real-time monitoring and controlling of the battery pack voltage and current for safe and efficient operation. State of charge (SOC) is the crucial factor for BMS. For accurate battery SOC estimation, battery pack modeling is required. In this work, the battery pack is modeled by Electrical Equivalent Circuit Model (1-RC model). The parameters of battery pack are estimated by Fixed Forgetting Factor Recursive Least Squares (RLS-FF) based on terminal voltage and load current data. There are number of methods that can be used for the estimation of SOC. Here, Kalman filter is used for SOC estimation. However, the drawback of Kalman filter is that it cannot estimate the initial SOC of the battery pack. This draw-back can be improved by using the relationship between SOC and Open circuit voltage (OCV) which has been implemented in this paper. The experiment is implemented in Arduino Mega 2560 microcontroller to make it cost-efficient, and the results are validated using Kalman filter block in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Structural Analysis of Slitted Rotor for 10,000 rpm Switched Reluctance Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Switched reluctance machines (SRMs) are increasingly being investigated for high-speed and high-temperature applications, as their rotors do not have permanent magnets or windings. Solid rotor SRMs are a viable option for high-speed and high-temperature applications. However, rotor core losses are quite high in solid rotor SRM. Recently, slitted rotor SRM has been proposed to reduce rotor core loss significantly compared to the solid rotor SRM. The slits are made in the active portion of the rotor perpendicular to the shaft axis to reduce the core losses. While this improves the electrical performance, the shaft rigidity and integrity are evaluated in this paper. Stress analysis and deformation due to the forces acting on the rotor at different speeds and load conditions are presented. The natural frequencies of the slitted rotor and corresponding mode shapes are determined using model analysis. The first four natural frequencies are 885 Hz, 2363 Hz, 3592 Hz, and 4308 Hz. Further, a comparative study between slitted and solid rotors specifically designed for a 5 kW, 10000 rpm SRM is presented, offering insights into their respective performance characteristics.

articleTitle: Review of Present Status and Recent Development in Active Cell Balancing Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) prove to be a sustainable mode of transportation concerning environment friendliness and the limited reserve of petrol and diesel. Notably, a crucial constituent of an EV is the battery. So, it becomes significant to safeguard the battery and prolong its operational life. Battery Management Systems (BMS) is a smart technique employed in EVs that manages and controls the charging and discharging operations of batteries. Cell Balancing (CB) is an imperative function of the BMS that maximizes battery efficiency by balancing the State Of Charge (SOC) levels and consequently the voltages of the cells in a battery pack. CB phenomenon is broadly classified into the Passive Cell Balancing (PCB) and Active Cell Balancing (ACB) strategies. PCB strategy involves the expulsion of charge from higher SOC cells to the connected dissipative resistors for balancing its SOC as per the lower SOC cells. This technique is usually preferred for low-power applications involving low cost. However, for high-power applications, it necessitates the use of the ACB strategy where charge from higher SOC cells is disseminated among the lower SOC cells so that the SOC of all the cells balances to an average SOC value. As a result, the battery run time can be augmented and that would extend the driving range of an EV. This work focuses on reviewing the different ACB strategies of BMS that can be successfully used for EV s.

articleTitle: Autoencoders for Compressed Transmission of Vehicular Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: V2V(vehicle-to-vehicle) communication has many applications with regard to intelligent transportation systems(ITS), accident prevention, traffic detection, etc. One of the major challenges in V2V communication is the data transmission in high mobility and bandwidth bottlenecks. CAM (cooperative awareness messages), messages are transmitted at a very high rate to update LDM (local dynamic map) to get better traffic awareness. CAM uses broadcast messaging. This could overload the communication network in a dense traffic scenario. In this paper, a data compression framework using the transmission of autoencoder(AE) models in vehicular sensor networks is proposed, where the comparable AE variants are analyzed. The accelerometer and gyrometer data have been used for analysis and the evaluation of the AE variants is performed. The simulation results show the superior performance of the denoising AE. Security is also a concern in transmitting sensor data to other vehicles. The proposed method adds an extra layer of security due to the transmission of AE models in the initialization phase.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Analysis of GPS Spoofing Attack Failures Using Poisson Point Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This study presents a geospatial analysis approach to derive the failure probability of GPS spoofing attacks by utilizing Poisson Point Process (PPP) modeling. The research begins by establishing a robust framework for characterizing GPS spoofing attacks based on available data and historical attack patterns. Leveraging the PPP model, which is commonly used in spatial point process analysis, the study integrates real-world information such as GPS receiver locations, environmental conditions, and spoofing device parameters to simulate the spatial distribution of spoofing attack attempts across a given area. Through the application of PPP modeling, the study aims to estimate the failure probability of GPS spoofing attacks, which is defined as the likelihood of the spoofer's signal being successfully received and accepted by a targeted GPS receiver. This approach allows for the incorporation of various geospatial factors, including receiver density, signal propagation, and environmental interference, to provide a more accurate representation of the vulnerability of the GPS system to spoofing attacks in specific geographic areas. The findings from this research are expected to contribute to enhancing the understanding of GPS vulnerability and improving countermeasures against spoofing attacks. The closed form expression for GPS Spoofing attack failure probability is derived using the Poisson point process. The simulation is compared with the theoretical results and observed that it is exactly close to each other.

articleTitle: Approximation of Grid Connected Higher Order Wind Turbine Generator System Employing Direct Truncation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The presented research article is providing the approximation of mathematically modelled higher order wind turbine generator (HOWTG) system. The modelling of eighth order WTG system is formulated by utilizing system parameters value, primarily. Then, the eighth order HOWTG is approximated to comparatively lower order (LO) WTG model. The approximation of HOWTG is done with the help of direct truncation (DT) approximation approach. The truncated second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh order LOWTG models are proposed for HOWTG system. To determine the best suited LOWTG model for HOWTG system, the obtained results are supported by findings and discussion in the terms of plots and tabulated data. The step response, error plot, and Bode plot are provided to highlight the compatibility of approximated LOWTG model with respect to HOWTG system. The approximated models are also compared with respect to HOWTG by considering time domain specifications and error index values in this contribution.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Grid Interfaced PV-BS System with Enhanced Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This article proposes an adaptive affine projection (AAP) algorithm based control technique for a three phase grid connected photovoltaic battery storage (GCPBS) system. The loads connected at the point of common coupling are mainly fed by the PV, and the absence of PVis compensated by the battery. Similarly, the excess generation of PV is fed to the battery and the grid. This PV intermittency and nonlinear loads cause power quality (PQ) issues. To address these issues, the proposed AAP based control technique generates a sinusoidal reference current by extracting the weight component of the load current. Furthermore, the proposed control approach effectively maintains the power flow in the system and mitigates grid current harmonics, thereby improving the grid PQ. Additionally, proper power balance is maintained irrespective of dynamic conditions and enhances the battery life simultaneously. The performance of the proposed control technique is evaluated by simulating in the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: AEFA-Enhanced Design for Optimized FODD
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this article, an efficient approach for designing fractional order digital differentiators (FODDs) of both second and fifth orders using the powerful meta heuristic Artificial Electric Field Algorithm (AEF A) is proposed. AEFA simulates the fundamental principles of electrostatic force, as described by Coulomb's law, and the laws of motion established by Newton. The performance metric used for evaluating the quality of designed FODDs is the Mean Absolute Relative Magnitude Error (MARME). The experimental results highlight the exceptional efficacy of AEFA in addressing complex FODD design problems, with the obtained solutions significantly outperforming existing cutting-edge methods.

articleTitle: Power Flow Analysis of 2×27.5 kV Traction Network with Single-Phase Transformer and V/V Transformer at Traction Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Determination of system variables such as voltage, currents etc., is a vital part of the planning and operation of the traction network. These system variables are further used for the design and condition monitoring of the traction network. In this study, to determine these system variables, the load flow analysis of the 2 × 27.5 k V traction network has been performed with a single-phase transformer and V/V connected transformer at the traction substation (TSS). Further, the voltage unbalance introduced at the grid side of the TSS has been analysed for these two different TSS transformers.

articleTitle: Convolution Neural Network for Fault Detection and Classification in Hybrid Overhead-Underground Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In distribution systems, a trend to use overhead (OH) lines along with underground (UG) cable is becoming popular due to densely populated areas which give rise to right of way and public safety issues. In these complex systems, maintaining continuous power supply and early detection and clearance of the fault are challenging tasks. Feature extraction from fault signals is the main concern of all detection schemes during occurrence of a fault. This article presents a Convolution Neural Network (CNN) which is a single learning body to detect faults in hybrid OH-UG cable. CNN rules are superior to other pattern-recognition techniques since they extract features and simultaneously detect faults as a single entity. The hybrid distribution system is simulated using MATLAB and the proposed scheme is compared with different soft computing techniques.

articleTitle: Inductor Current Harmonic Analysis in DC-DC Dual Active Bridge Converter with Various Control Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Dual active bridge converter is widely used in electric vehicle charging infrastructure, Data centers etc. due to the added advantages of inherent soft-switching, galvanic isolation and bidirectional power flow capability. Power flow is controlled by changing the phase shift angle between switching pulses of primary and secondary side converters. In this paper, design considerations of dual active bridge are presented along with different phase shift control techniques such as Single phase shift, Extended phase shift and Dual phase shift control technique and are compared on the basis of total harmonic distortion of the inductor current waveform which contributes to higher device stress and losses. Maximum achievable load with the given switching frequency and inductance is determined for optimized performance of the converter. The performance comparison of various control techniques have been performed in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Half Bridge Compensator Design for THD Reduction and DC Link Voltage Stabilisation of Electric Traction
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Railway power conditioners have played a vital role in the railway industry by compensating negative sequence current (NSC), reactive power and current harmonics. Also, various power conditioners have been framed to ease its implementation and improve the power quality of the traction system. To nullify the power quality problem in the railway power supply network, a railway static power conditioner (RPC) based on a half-bridge converter is proposed. Compared with conventional Half-Bridge-Converter-Based Railway Static Power Conditioners, the proposed conditioner could reduce the rating and cost of power quality conditioner. Cooperative control strategies have been developed to achieve accurate tracking of reference signals.

articleTitle: Research and Evaluate the Impact of Electric Vehicle Integration in Microgrid on Bach Long Vy Island, Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Green energy is a significant concern recently attracting worldwide attention. Using renewable energy sources and vehicles such as Electric Vehicles (EVs) has solved the problem of environmental pollution. However, the integration of electric vehicles into the Microgrid (MG) has caused some negative impacts on the way the grid operates. Bach Long Vy Island is one of Vietnam's most beautiful tourist islands. Besides, this is the Island with the most modern MG in Southeast Asia, so in the future, the number of EVs will increase on the Island. The article focuses on building an MG model that integrates electric vehicle loads in MATLAB software. Research the ability to meet load demand based on analysis of parameters such as voltage quality, frequency, and power. Several EV charging scenarios were tested based on Vinfast's actual charging model. Thereby, review and evaluate the feasibility of MG with the development of EVs in Vietnam shortly.

articleTitle: Analysis of Non-Isolated Dual Output Tristate Converter for Low Voltage DC Bus
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this paper, a DC-DC Non-Isolated Single Input Dual Output (NI-SIDO) architecture with tri-state configuration is laid out, which is designed to provide both step-up and step-down outputs. The problem related to stability is mitigated by using tristate configuration in the presented NI-SIDO converter. The system is divided into three sub-systems having DC-DC tri-state boost converter and NI-SIDO converter as source converters and DC-DC buck converter acting as a load converter regulated using voltage loop control. The presented system performance and results are validated using MATLAB/SIMULINK software.

Author Keywords: DC-DC Single Input Dual Output (SIDO) Converter

articleTitle: Sizing and Performance Analysis of a Battery Energy Storage System in Bangladesh Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper aims to evaluate and determine the appropriate size of a battery energy storage system within Bangladesh's distribution system. The country frequently experiences load shedding due to a substantial in-crease in local loads, particularly during peak hours. A larger-scale lithium battery bank, independent of any generating sources connected to the grid, could be an excellent solution. An optimal strategy is devised to identify the most suitable lo-cation for establishing the battery bank, considering the check and balance between the required load demand and the grid's integrity and reliability. This system has a minimum cost and ensures a probability of loss of power supply (PLPS) below 5%. For the case study, a comprehensive power network in Bangladesh is simulated using the ETAP platform to analyze the system's sizing and performance compared to other models. As a result, a substantial enhancement in the power system's reliability and quality is achieved cost-effectively.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of False Data Injection Attacks on the Energy Market
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The False Data Injection Attack (FDIA) has emerged as a significant cybersecurity threat to modern power systems. This insidious attack has the potential to manipulate state estimation outcomes arbitrarily, all while evading detection by traditional bad data detectors. Beyond the risks of causing physical damage, attackers can exploit FDIA for financial gains. The profound effects of FDI attacks on the functioning of the energy market are examined in this work. False Data Injection attacks include inserting malicious data into market systems with the intention of changing important parameters and interfering with the market's regular operation. This work focuses on the intentional manipulation of Locational Marginal Prices (LMPs) in the power system via False Data Injection (FDI) attacks. LMPs at individual buses are manipulated in order to track and measure the direct impact on market operations. This research is carried out to know the FDIA impacts on energy markets on realistic modern power systems. The paper unveils the susceptibility of energy markets to FDIA.By providing useful insights into reducing the risks associated with Locational Marginal Price manipulation and preserving the integrity of state estimation processes, this research makes a significant contribution to the field of power system security.

articleTitle: Analysis, Design, and Control of the Dual Active Bridge Converter for EV Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The growing demand for electric vehicles (EVs) has increased the need for high-quality EV battery chargers. The dual active bridge (DAB) converter, with its safety features like high-frequency galvanic isolation and bidirectional power flow, has become a promising solution for efficient EV battery charging. This paper explores the mathematical modeling, control, and design of the DAB converter-based EV battery charging system under different operating conditions. In order to regulate the power transfer, a single-phase shift (SPS) modulation strategy is employed during constant current (CC) /constant voltage (CV) charging modes. A prototype scaled model rated at 24W is developed in the laboratory environment with operating frequency of 10kHz and tested under varying supply conditions.

articleTitle: XAI-Driven sEMG Feature Analysis for Hand Gestures
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) signals play a vital role in hand gesture recognition for identifying various hand movements. Due to its non-invasive nature and real-time muscle activation detection capabilities, sEMG is widely employed in hand gesture identification. The utilization of Machine Learning (ML) for real-time recognition of sEMG-based hand gestures is an emerging and evolving field. Along with this, the ML classifiers are also known as “black boxes” since they cannot provide discernible insights into how decisions are produced and what factors impact them. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is employed to emphasize the importance of specific features in machine learning models. In this study, employed data related to six hand gestures to assess the performance of five different machine learning models. Among these classifiers, the Extra Tree model demonstrated the highest accuracy, achieving an impressive 85.22%. Furthermore, the XAI-LIME model has been employed to investigate these models' feature relevance for all six hand gestures under examination.

articleTitle: An Improved Ultra High Gain Quadratic Boost Converter With Classical Voltage Doubler Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this paper, a modified ultra-high gain DC-DC boost converter has been proposed. The proposed converter has improved the performance of the conventional converter by increasing the voltage gain 2.34 times that of the conventional converter by adding a classical doubler circuit (2 capacitors and 2 diodes) in the design structure. In addition, the continuous input current features are retained in the proposed structure. The steady-state modeling, including the operating principles and the stress calculation of the components, has been illustrated. The proposed model has been simulated in Matlab/Simulink software with proper component specification. The simulation's results validate the correctness of the proposed converter by aligning well with the findings of the mathematical computation.

articleTitle: Performance of Single-Stage and Dual-Stage EV Battery Chargers for G2V and V2G Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In recent years the growth of electric vehicles has increased day by day and this encourages the different G2V, V2G, V2V, V2L, and V2H technologies. In this paper, discussed the bidirectional power flow from the grid to the vehicle or vice versa. V2G technology is very beneficial during peak load periods, voltage regulation, and improvement of power system stability. To implement this V2G technology, it required proper management of the electric battery charger and the charger is capable of flowing the power in either direction. This paper shows the single-stage and dual-stage charger topology to flow the power in either direction i.e. G2V or V2G. This paper also shows the battery can be charged using constant current and constant voltage charging methods. In the single stage, use only the PFC circuit to charge or discharge the battery. In the dual-stage, an active bridge rectifier for AC to DC conversion with an L filter in series with the source has been used and for the next stage, a bidirectional DAB converter with an LC filter for DC to DC conversion is used and a separate control strategy for battery charging & discharging. This paper shows the battery control strategy can charge or discharge the battery at constant current and constant voltage. The performance of this single-stage and dual-stage battery charger is verified by simulations in MATLAB/SIMULINK software and the waveform is verified in real-time using the OPAL-RT system.

articleTitle: Power Management of Novel DC-DC Converter for Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper conceptualizes the power management of a novel DC-DC converter for microgrid application. The novel DC-DC converter is a voltage multiplier based high gain multiport non-isolated converter; with two output ports of different voltage levels. The novel DC-DC converter has a voltage gain of 15 to achieve high gain operation. The output voltage levels at 1500 V & 1385 V are suitable for DC Microgrid, MVDC distribution, EV charging, commercial & industrial DC loads, etc. The converter's operation in different scenarios is analyzed for duty ratio control with steady-state equations and necessary waveforms. A closed loop control of the novel DC-DC converter is proposed to monitor optimal power management of the resources and loads. The main objective is to achieve steady output port voltages during dynamic conditions under the proposed control scheme; which was not achievable with duty ratio control hence, validating results in MATLAB/Simulink are presented.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Microgrid System with Active Load in Autonomous Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper deals with the analysis of the stability of a microgrid (MG) system providing power to both passive and active loads. Constant power loads are reasons for the unstable operation of microgrid as it demonstrates negative impedance characteristics. However, they stabilize the microgrid system when operated in parallel with a constant impedance load. The presence of an active load affects the power demand, voltage regulation, energy efficiency, and reliability of the microgrid. Rectifier or voltage regulator type loads in microgrid degrade the small signal damping as their control loop dynamics is in sync with the frequency range of inverters deployed. In this paper, participation analysis of the eigenvalues of the system with active load identifies the low-frequency modes which are associated with the voltage controller of the active load. While further analysis shows the active load voltage controller with large gains, affects the performance of the voltage controller of the inverters connected to the system. The whole system model is developed in MATLAB, where the voltage, frequency, and real and reactive power profiles are studied to understand the effect of active load.

articleTitle: Prediction of Bevel-Tip Needle Deflection Using CART Based Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Minimal-invasive surgery has gained popularity due to reduced blood loss, minimal patient discomfort, lower costs, and faster recovery. However, its success relies heavily on the needle tip's precision. The interaction between the needle and tissue notably influences this accuracy. Achieving a significant degree of accuracy is challenging because of the uncertain mechanics and the varying stiffness of heterogeneous tissue. The foremost factor influencing the misplacement of a needle is deflection. Therefore, this research paper introduces a machine learning approach for predicting needle deflection. The machine learning method such as a decision tree, is utilized and trained using collected experimental data. Decisions, such as determining which feature contributes more to deflection, are made without depending on any mathematical model.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Nine Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Using electric motors with a phase greater than three present some advantages over conventional three phase machines: higher reliability, reduced power per phase, increased torque density, and reduced torque pulsations. A nine-phase inverter implies 512 switching vectors in each one of its four harmonic planes. Recently, model predictive control (MPC) has attracted a wide attention in area of power converters and drives due to its various advantages like that of several control targets, variables and constraints can be included in single cost function and simultaneously controlled. Consequently, in this article performance of model predictive control is studied within the context of a nine-phase system. The motor is driven by a nine-phase power supply system, which means it has nine distinct windings or phases instead of the typical three in a three-phase system. This allows for more precise control of the motor's torque and speed, as well as better performance in terms of torque ripple reduction and efficiency. This article explores the principles and advantages of nine-phase MPC, particularly in applications such as robotics, electric vehicles, and industrial automation where high precision and dynamic performance are crucial.

articleTitle: A Grid-Connected Hybrid System Utilizing Solar & Waste of Chattogram City
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Bangladesh is an agricultural-based country whose economy depends upon its agriculture. However, ur-banization and industrialization have changed over recent years. Therefore, it is now experiencing an acute electric power shortage and growing demand. So development is ham-pered because the Government does not mitigate this amount of demand. To minimize this demand, the Govern-ment proposed some mega-projects, such as nuclear, oil, and coal-based power plants in different parts of the country, which are conventional. Moreover, the nuclear power plant is un-suitable for overcoming this situation and requires higher safety facilities. So, N onconventional energy is the ultimate choice to reduce the power crisis because energy re-sources (solar, waste) are available in Bangladesh (city, rural) areas. For that reason, to reduce carbon emissions and meet en-ergy demands, a grid-connected solar and municipal waste biomass-based hybrid system has been proposed to mitigate the rising electricity demand in Bangladesh city corporation ar-eas. Patenga, Chittagong area, was chosen for the case study, where the solar source is excellent, and the availability of solid waste is remarkable.

articleTitle: TPUPS Topology Implemented with Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Due to the expansion of the power electronics industry, DC-DC converters have been in demand for the last 20 years. Multi-port converters are studied and used because of the use of numerous sources or loads in microgrids. An uninterruptible power supply with several ports has been addressed in this proposed study. As the name implies, this system continuously feeds to load in hybrid mode. These converters are among the most effective available today. In this work, a battery backup port is added, and a DC grid is employed as the primary power source. Battery is used as bidirectional load/source that's charging and discharging mode both observed. Battery is charged through a CC/CV charge controller. In this proposed system converter is designed such that it can be modified later by adding more source or load. Model predictive controllers are used for control purposes. To produce the desired output, this controller relies on the principles of optimization and prediction. Hence, the importance of the cost function is addressed for several scenarios. Model predictive control is one of the most reliable and simple control methods for multi-port converters.

articleTitle: Regularized Hybrid Deep Learning for DDoS Attack Prediction in Software Defined Internet of Things (SD-IoT)
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The availability of online resource is seriously threatened by the fatal DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks, which can earnestly break up a targeted network or website by flooding it with traffic. DDoS attacks can use a variety of tactics and can be launched from different points around the world, making it difficult to predict when they will occur. In order to improve accuracy by minimizing overfitting of data in CNN, this work proposes an efficient method by combining CNN with Bi-LSTM for predicting DDoS attacks based on a modified loss function with regularization. We test our method on the CICDDOS2019 dataset of network traffic and demonstrate that it can accurately and successfully predict DDoS attacks with an accuracy of 99.8% and an F-score of 97.29%.

articleTitle: LSTM Classifier Based Fault Detection and Classification Scheme for 1-Open Conductor Faults in Six-Phase Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: As the demand for electrical energy grows by the day, bulk power transmission is the primary concern for power system planners. Six-phase transmission lines are capable of carrying 1.732 times more power than three-phase double-circuit transmission lines with the prevailing right of way. However, due to the large number of faults, identification of faults is a critical task in the six-phase system. In this context, this work proposes a straightforward and practical solution to the complex fault classification problem. The use of Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) for 1-Open conductor problems resulted in a high degree of accuracy in fault identification and classification. The efficacy of the current classifier has been tested for various 1-Open conductor faults with a wide range of fault attributes. The validation results of LSTM based fault classifier shows that the method can detect and identify the phase involved in the fault. In addition, the method is robust to changes in the fault attributes.

Author Keywords: Long short term memory based fault detector/classifier

articleTitle: Environment-Friendly Economic Load Dispatch Using a Novel GSA-BBO Hybridization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In order to address environment-friendly economic load dispatch problems, a unique hybrid algorithm based on Newton's law of gravity and biogeography is suggested in this study. It expands the search space of the Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA) from a local population range to a global scale by incorporating the principles of biogeography employed in the case of Biogeography Based Optimization (BBO). The enhanced search capability of GSA-BBO is effectively utilized in this paper to achieve multiple objectives. Validation is conducted on an IEEE 30-bus system. The findings acquired through the GSA-BBO are being compared to the results obtained through other approaches mentioned in the literature. It demonstrates the computational capabilities and consistency of GSA-BBO, confirming its efficacy and reliability.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Modified Three Phase Symmetric Five Level Inverter For Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Worldwide Industrial revolution requires high demand of power which has already kicked off the research on power conversion from renewable sources to conventional grid system. With a view to facilitating this research, Multilevel Inverters (MLI) are futuristic industrial solution. Multilevel inverters represent a pivotal advancement in power electronics technology, transforming the way we generate and control electrical energy. The key objective of the conducted research is to suggest a novel and modified three phase symmetric five level inverter with Low THD and minimum switch count. The proposed topology reduces the number of diodes, capacitors and switches compared to existing MLI topologies. It also demonstrates satisfactory performance in terms of reduced number of switching devices, DC sources, minimum blocking voltage, power rating of the devices and costs. MATLAB/Simulink was used to design and assess dynamic performance of the proposed topology based on variations of dynamic loads for high and medium voltage applications.

articleTitle: Non-singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Crack Sealing Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this work, the branch of the tree robot has been controlled for crack sealing of concrete pipe. This tree robot is used for repair and maintenance purposes. It can maneuvers inside vertical pipes, horizontal pipes and surfaces. A CAD model of the pipe is modelled in Solidworks, and a mimic of the existing crack is simulated inside the pipes. Furthermore, the crack repair has been assured for the branch of the tree robot. However, due to the presence of uncertainty and disturbances, the end-effector of the tree robot doesn't follow the desired crack trajectory. Sliding mode control (SMC) is a well-known method to address such types of problems. But, conventional SMC solved one aspect of the problem. Therefore, The Non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (NFTSMC) is proposed for this work since it ensures fast convergence in finite time. After performing the simulation and numerous iterations, it is found that the NFTSMC gives a more promising result compared to SMC with constant plus proportional reaching law (CPPRL). Furthermore, the work exploits the Lyapunov candidate function to ensure the asymptotic stability of the crack trajectory.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Enhancement for EV Stations: An Optimal Mechanism Utilizing a Smart Solar Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The rapid growth of Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations has raised concerns about their impact on grid stability. This paper presents a study on integrating PV Systems with smart inverters in EV charging stations to enhance grid stability and energy efficiency. Two scenarios are analyzed: one without smart inverters and one with their integration. In the absence of smart inverters, charging events are poorly aligned with energy supply, resulting in voltage fluctuations, grid instability, and higher operational costs. However, the introduction of smart inverters significantly improves the situation. It optimizes charging operations, reduces energy waste, enhances grid stability, and minimizes voltage fluctuations. The proposed system's model and mechanism are comprehensively analyzed using the ETAP platform. This research underscores the vital role of smart inverters in promoting eco-friendly charging and improving overall grid stability in the context of EV charging stations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Hardware-in-Loop Testbed for Power System Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Modern power grid require an enhanced level of detail in order to properly represent their behavior due to its complex nature, new operation and management strategies need to be tested to ensure power system reliability and security. EMT-based real-time digital simulation allows to overcome these constraints which allows to obtain high precision results in a timeframe suited for online monitoring. The recent advancements in modeling, computing, and simulation technology has made it possible to shift the system analysis from offline to online with the help of EMT-based real-time platforms such as Opal-RT HYPERSIM. This bridges the gap between the real-time responses and the simulation environment using hardware-in-loop for complex systems. OPAL-RT HYPERSIM is used as a real-time simulation platform, entering into the world of Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulation. OPAL-RT enables the real-time connection of actual hardware with virtual models, facilitating the evaluation, improvement, and optimization of complex systems across several fields by engineers and researchers. HIL is an effective methodology for rigorous and dynamic system testing and demonstration that is challenging with other methodologies. This paper proposes the EMT-based RTHIL testbed, which includes all the essential industry hardware for testing and validating different scenarios. The IEEE 39 bus system is utilized as a use case, consisting of a substantial network with 39 nodes and 10 generator models, specifically for disturbance analysis. The HIL setup facilitates a comprehensive understanding of the consequences of various fault scenarios, providing accurate results.

articleTitle: High-Speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Design for Mini Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The rapid evolution of unmanned aerial vehicles (U A V s) has led to an increased demand for efficient and reliable propulsion systems. This study focuses on the design and development of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) specifically designed for mini unmanned aerial vehicles. The designed PMSM has been designed to deliver 300 W output power, produce 0.28 Nm torque and operate at 10110 rpm with 28V DC supply voltage. Spoke type rotor has been preferred in PMSM design. This design not only ensures magnet integrity under high rotation speeds, but also increases the flux density in the air gap, significantly increasing torque output. Improved torque output contributes to the UAV's maneuverability, allowing rapid adaptation to evolving mission demands.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Routing Techniques using Sink Mobility Models for IoT assisted WSN
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Improving network lifetime with energy-efficient utilization is the main aim of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) design. Sink mobility is an effective strategy for increasing performance in WSNs, such as easing traffic stress from sensor nodes. WSN routing protocols are categorized into distinct groups depending on their network topology and suitability. In this research article, we have analyzed the performance of various WSN routing protocols such as DIRECT, LEACH, PEGASIS, MR-LEACH, and EEUCLC under the following mobile sink locations. We assumed three sink positions for static sink scenarios: center, corner, and outside the Region of Interest (RoI). Random, grid, spiral, and Gaussian models have been used for the mobile sink. For a large-scale WSN, multi-hopping and unequal clustering is an effective mechanisms for improving the network performance. However, to further improve the efficiency, sink mobility is an efficient method for enhancing the execution of WSNs as it avoids creating energy holes/hot spots by avoiding long-distance transmissions in those areas. It is found through our simulation that by using random and deterministic mobility patterns, energy efficiency improves by 7%-10%.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Various Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper examines several sinusoidal pulse-width modulation (SPWM) methods for single-phase H-Bridge inverters. Various SPWM strategies have been proposed in the literature up to this point. With PWM, the inverter's output voltage can be changed, so large filters are no longer needed. The conventional and modified SPWM techniques are described in this paper. Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), switching losses, fundamental component values, and dead time losses are used to compare the effectiveness of these SPWM methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Transformer Reliability through Machine Learning-Based Fault Prediction Using Dissolved Gas Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The global energy sector operates within a highly competitive market, necessitating uninterrupted power supply to industrial, commercial, and domestic sectors. Transformers serve a critical role in electricity transmission, emphasizing the importance of maintaining their performance to minimize losses. Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) emerges as a pivotal tool for monitoring transformer performance and identifying fault types in oil-immersed transformers. Despite the existence of several conventional DGA interpretation techniques, their accuracy has been subpar. This research paper presents a novel machine learning(ML) approach for predicting power transformer faults using DGA data. The proposed method leverages DGA samples sourced from the IEEE data port to train and test various machine learning models within the WEKA platform.

articleTitle: Application of DG Droop Equations for State Estimation of Islanded AC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The islanded mode of AC Microgrids (IMGs) plays a crucial role in enhancing the reliability and resilience of power systems. Accurate state estimation is essential for optimal operation and control of IMGs. This paper proposes a new approach for state estimation of IMGs by incorporating distributed generators (DGs) droop equations into the widely used weighted least squares (WLS) method. The proposed methodology was more effective regarding initialization and measurement noise issues observed with conventional WLS methods. The developed SE algorithm was validated on a large-scale 906-bus IM G system, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving state estimation accuracy. The findings indicate that the proposed method can significantly reduce estimation errors compared to the conventional WLS method used for the SE of IMG.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Solar Powered EV with Transformerless Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have become a popular trend in modern times due to their numerous benefits such as the use of renewable energy instead of conventional fuel. When designing the EV architecture, selecting the appropriate DC-DC converter topology is crucial. These converters are essential for matching input voltage with system requirements and controlling power flow. In this study, a high voltage gain Transformerless Buck-Boost converter was chosen for the EV system, which demonstrated high efficiency and minimal power loss. The source for the converter was obtained from solar panels and the MPPT controller was employed for converter control. The performance of the selected converter topology was compared with that of the conventional Buck-Boost converter and Boost converter because these two converters are mainly used in EV systems. The analysis showed that the transformer-less buck-boost converter[2] performed better than the conventional buck-boost converter. The simulation of these converters was carried out using MATLAB Simulink and the results were verified. In conclusion, the chosen converter topology offers improved performance and efficiency, making it a suitable choice for EV systems that use renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: A Simulation Analysis of 30 kV / 5A DC Power Supply for Neutral Beam Injectors
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The demand for high-voltage DC power supplies in particle accelerators and other research applications necessitates the development of reliable and efficient power supplies capable of delivering stable DC voltage and current outputs. This paper presents the basic design and simulation of a 30 kV., 5 A DC power supply for feeding the accelerator grids of neutral beam injectors (NBI). The key attributes of these power supplies are their low ripple content., low stored energy., and fast turn-on and fast turn-off which are highly essential for the successful operation of the NBI. A modular concept-based topology is proposed in which the power supply has been designed for varying the output voltbage over a wide range., from 10 % to 100 % of its rated output voltage by using the pulse width modulation (PWM) technique. The simulation results of the designed power supply are presented which have been carried out using MATLAB/Simulink. The results include both the steady state and dynamic response of the system along with fault analysis. All the technical requirements of the power supply were compiled through the simulation study.

articleTitle: Application of Wide Bandgap Devices in a Three-Level Neutral Point Clamped Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Wide Bandgap (WBG) Devices have brought significant advancements in the field of power electronics due to their remarkable advantages such as high switching frequency, low conduction loss and improved thermal performance. The objective of this paper is to investigate the potential of integrating these devices into a three-level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) inverter that is connected to the electrical grid. This integration is of significant importance in today's power system to improve energy conversion systems and also to meet the growing need for more efficient and versatile power systems, enhancing the resilience of modern power grids. The process of conducting simulations is accomplished through the use of the PLECS.

articleTitle: Breaking New Ground: High-Accuracy Detection and Severity Analysis of Onion Smut Using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Finding and putting plant diseases in the right category is very important for farming ways. It directly affects how you look after your plants and the food they give. In this work, a mixed deep learning (DL) model is made and tested to directly deal with the problem of finding out onion smut disease. This new study puts together the strong power that Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have with the powerful ability to sort things out which Support Vector Machines (SVM) possess. For the sickness's seriousness, this method can place onion smut into six separate groups. When tested on 2600 real-time pictures, the model got an overall correctness of 92%. This clearly shows that it is good at finding diseases correctly and also figuring out how bad they are. The study shows that this mixed CNN-SVM model is much better than the old ways of making things right. In the future, farming and plant care will be a helpful tool for doing jobs very accurately. This job is helpful for the farming area of artificial intelligence (AI). It also shows how future studies can use a mix of machine learning and sorting techniques to group plant illnesses.

articleTitle: Intelligent Adaptive Control of Magnetically Growing Rod-Like System
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper represents on intelligent adaptive control of magnetic controlled growing rods (MGCR) which used in the treatment of early-onset scoliosis. With intelligent adaptive control theory system can be controlled precisely when system includes high order non-linearities or uncertainties. Radial basis functions (RBF)-based neuron structure continuously update itself with online learning model for the reason of dynamic responses to the system behaviour. Therefore, robust control of the system against all kinds of variable conditions can be achieved. In the context of this scholarly paper, a configuration akin to that of MCGR has been devised to serve as the experimental setup. Additionally, this setup includes uncertainties and non-linearities, the same as in a real system, which is an opportunity to analyse the robustness and adaptivity of control theory.

articleTitle: Dual Input Step-up Converter for Portable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper comprehensively analyses a Dual-Input Step-Up DC-DC Converter, a crucial component in both renewable energy systems and portable electronic devices. It also provides a detailed mathematical model of the converter and supports its performance with experimental data. The examination includes efficiency and thermal characteristics to ensure optimal operation. One of the key advantages of the dual-input configuration is its ability to integrate various energy sources, enhancing versatility seamlessly. Efficiency analysis covers Duty ratio and load conditions. Additionally, thermal analysis sheds light on heat management, a critical aspect of ensuring reliability. The background underscores the growing demand for efficient energy conversion in today's electronics and renewable energy applications. Dual-input converters address the challenge of integrating diverse energy sources, making a thorough analysis essential for widespread adoption. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for designing and optimizing dual-input step-up converters, contributing to advancements in the field of power electronics.

articleTitle: Detection of Industrial Motor Fault using Signal Processing Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Induction motors are the most commonly used motor in petrochemicals, agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, cement, steel, and many other process industries. A failure of any single component or sub-components of the induction motor can result in a plant shutdown. Hence, it is crucial to diagnose different types of faults in induction motors. The current study overviews a vibration-based condition monitoring method for detecting bent shaft failures in large industrial induction motors. This four-pole, 1.7-MW induction motor is primarily utilized in the petrochemical sector. A bent shaft is a typical problem with the motor's rotational portion. A bent shaft creates excessive vibration in a machine depending on the extent and position of the bend. This present study uses vibration data samples collected during the last four years. The data is collected from the deteriorating status of the induction motor. As the vibration signal of the corresponding data sets is non-stationary time-frequency domain analysis is mainly used. Several types of failures happened in various frequency sub-bands of an induction motor. As a result, the discrete wavelet transform is primarily utilized to detect defective frequency ranges. The objective of this study is to use discrete wavelet transform based vibration analysis to check if there is a trend in percentage energy and, if so, to identify the frequency range of the bent shaft issue of an induction motor. In discrete wavelet transform analysis, the detail sub-band-1 shows the deteriorating condition of an induction motor. The frequency range of detail sub-band-l is 1280 Hz to 2560 Hz. On the time-frequency plots, more precise detection of frequency range may be obtained. If the vibration is increased from the lowest to highest peak value in a time-frequency plot, the corresponding energy likewise attempts to locate compactly in discrete bits.

articleTitle: ECG Signal Denoising Using Sparrow Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a wave portrayal of the electrical representation of heart function that offers important details of the heart's rhythms. It diagnoses cardiac problems by detecting the heart's electrical functioning. While recording the original ECG signal, some noise is added. Therefore, it is rational to rebuild the signal by reducing noise. This work describes an ECG signal denoising technique that employs the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) and is based on the finite impulse response (FIR) filtering approach. Performance measures such as mean difference (MD), normalized root mean square error (NRMSE), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), mean square error (MSE) and correlation coefficient (CC) are computed to validate the findings. The experimental results demonstrate that using SSA has obtained better performance compare to other method.

articleTitle: Energy Highway: A Community-Centric Approach for Decentralized Green Energy Exchange and Self-Sufficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The rise of distributed energy sources (DERs) has reshaped the dynamics of the energy market, leading to several intriguing research works on community-based energy exchanges. However, implementations of energy-sharing methods remain sparse in the existing literature. We propose a practical application of sharing model named as energy highway that allows community prosumers to trade green energy via existing grid infrastructure. To improve the system's integrity and transparency, we propose the use of blockchain and IoT devices to authenticate all green energy produced by prosumers. The billing structure of all valid energy transactions are computed by the grid service operator (GSO) via cloud services.
