Moreover, we have proposed a mechanism employing smart meters to monitor energy for each household. All houses engaging in the community's peer-to-peer (P2P) trading scheme receive financial advantages. We propose incentives to promote green energy exchanges within the community that not only spurs the adoption of more renewable systems but also boost interest in P2P energy exchange. Our ultimate goal is for a community to be self-sufficient through the independent generation and utilization of green energy, minimizing the dependence on external grid energy supply.

articleTitle: A Novel Non-Isolated High-Gain Boost DC- DC Converter with Single Switch and Minimum Component Count
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-isolated unidirectional DC-DC converter aimed to achieve substantial voltage gain while minimizing component stress and maintaining a low component count. The converter's architecture amalgamates modified Single-Ended Primary Inductance Converter (SEPIC) and traditional Cuk topologies, employing only a single switch. A comprehensive analysis of the derivation, operational principles, and steady-state characteristics of this novel converter is provided. Additionally, the paper encompasses dynamic modeling of the proposed converter and elucidates the design of closed-loop controllers tailored for current control modes. Extensive analysis and simulation results substantiate the effectiveness and performance of the proposed topology. This innovative converter offers a promising solution for efficient energy transfer, delivering exceptional voltage gain suitable across various applications.

articleTitle: Optimized Conductor Positioning for Three-Phase Double-Circuit Transmission Line to Reduce Line Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Multistart techniques are very useful in solving global optimization problems. Different algorithms and tools have evolved from the multistart approach to find optimal solutions to non-linear programming (NLP) problems. A modified version of the global search (MGS) toolbox is proposed here. MGS is applied to optimally reduce the capacitance of the transmission line. The algorithm is tested with three-phase double-circuit transmission lines with different voltage ratings, like 66 k V, 110 k V, etc.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Quadratic Boost Converter for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This work presents the implementation of a quadratic boost converter employing a proposed pulse skipping modulation-burst mode, specifically for light-load applications. The quadratic boost converter is recognized for its high-gain operation, making it well-suited for many power applications. However, achieving low losses under such load conditions is challenging, as efficiency tends to decrease at lighter loads due to significant switching losses (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{switch}$</tex>). The paper encompasses a theoretical analysis of the proposed approach, with simulations conducted in the MATLAB/Simulink environment to regulate output voltage. Simulation results demonstrate consistent regulation of voltage even when switching pulses are skipped using the proposed scheme. Additionally, the paper includes a theoretical analysis of inductor selection for Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM), where proposed scheme can be effectively adopted. To assess the feasibility of regulated output voltage during load steps transitions and input voltage transitions, the study conducts relevant experiments, revealing regulated output voltage with a ripple voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta v$</tex>) within the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 5mV$</tex>.

articleTitle: Stealthy False Data Injection Cyberattack Targeting Under Load Tap Changing Transformers in Smart Power Grid Causing Abnormal Voltage Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In the process of protecting power systems against different types of cyberattacks, the primary step is to precisely model such frameworks from attacker's perspective. This paper investigates a false data injection (FDI) attack framework, which can target under-load tap changing (ULTC) transformers, resulting in manipulated voltage profile in radial smart distribution networks. The developed FDI model compromises the voltage profile of a distribution feeder through misleading the volt/var optimization, that optimally manages system-wide voltage profile and flow of reactive power. The presented attack model is formulated as a bi-objective optimization problem. The objective functions from the attacker's point of view are 1) minimizing the level of false data to be injected into the smart meters associated with load data and 2) maximizing the voltage deviation of the distribution grid. Negative impacts of such a cyberattack model have been validated and discussed in this work on an IEEE distribution test system, necessitating proper remedial actions, which will be elaborated in the next step of this research.

articleTitle: Single-Phase Single-Stage Transformerless PV Inverter Used for the Minimization of Leakage Current in the Grid Connected Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper introduces a solution using a single-phase single-stage PV transformerless five-level inverter to address leakage current issues. By utilizing a single PV source, the proposed inverter generates five output voltage levels. The design involves cascading two converters to achieve the proposed single-phase single-stage PV transformerless five-level inverter. Operating in both buck and boost modes, the proposed single-phase single-stage PV transformerless five-level inverter demonstrates distinct output voltage peak values: matching the input PV voltage in buck mode and doubling the input PV voltage in boost mode. The paper elaborates on the switching states necessary to produce these five output voltage levels in both operational modes. The key innovation lies in maintaining a constant common-mode voltage, effectively reducing leakage current. This feature remains consistent in both buck and boost modes. Additionally, the paper includes simulation results validating the functionality of this proposed single-phase single-stage PV transformerless five-level inverter.

articleTitle: Optimal Load Prediction in a Smart Metering Network using Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Smart meters are electronic devices used to measure and record real-time energy consumption. In this research, we utilized energy consumption data gathered from residential consumers in London, England. Our aim is to leverage various machine learning algorithms to establish connections between historical energy consumption data, allowing us to create and assess short-term load forecasts with low Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). This research benefits customers by enabling them to plan their energy usage effectively, resulting in reduced overall energy bills. Our findings indicate that, among the tested algorithms, Random Forest stands out as the optimal choice, delivering the lowest RMSE and MAPE.

articleTitle: Peak Power Extraction from a PV System for Various DC and AC Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper describes the MPP determination of a photovoltaic (PV) panel using the explicit equation of current, which is only a function of voltage. Using an approximation of a straight line expression, the explicit equation of current is derived from implicit V-I characteristics. The V-I curves obtained from an implicit expression of current for various panel ratings are used to implement the proposed PV system expression of current. Under various environmental conditions (DEC), the proposed explicit V-I expression is used to directly estimate the MPP of a PV system. Using the MATLAB program, the MPP of the panel at DEC obtained by applying the proposed algorithm is contrasted with various existing techniques. The estimated MPP of a panel using the developed method closely matches the actual MPP values, according to the results. Additionally, there is little (%) error between estimated peak power using the developed method and measured peak power. As a result, a panel's estimated MPP calculated using the developed method is more precise.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of CMV Variation Using Different BUS Clamping SVPWM Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper compares the different bus clamping techniques with the 240° Space Vector PWM technique having load connected as inverter fed three-phase induction motor. It mainly focuses on reduction of number of switching in three phase, switching loss of inverter and also reduction in common mode voltage magnitude and frequency. As the switching loss reduces, the efficiency of the whole drive improves. This paper also provides a comparative analysis of their common mode voltage values and their respective THD's at different modulation indices along with number of switchings in each phase. It also shows the variation of load torque and its effects on THD at fixed modulation index. The comparative analysis is carried out among Conventional SVPWM, 30°, 60°, 120° and 240° bus clamping PWM techniques using SVPWM approach in a three-phase 2 level inverter driven 10 HP induction motor.

articleTitle: Image Segmentation Using Particle Swarm Optimization and Simulated Annealing
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A significant amount of picture segmentation is necessary for the accurate identification and diagnosis of the object of interest present in the image. Low image contrast and poorly defined boundaries are the problems of automatic segmentation. While there are many other picture segmentation techniques available, classic approaches are still popular despite having significant limitations that prevent them from producing reliable results. The main objective of this paper is to segment objects in an image by applying combined optimization techniques namely Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). PSO's worldwide exploration capability and SA's local refinement capability were combined for more effective segmentation. We also investigated, how the change of cluster size affects the output and the quality metrics. An increase in cluster size does not increase the quality metrics, instead, segmentation accuracy is increased based on the proper selection of cluster size. PSO-SA method is applied to different datasets, and segmentation accuracy is measured using several metrics namely precision, recall, F1 score, dice, and jaccard similarity.

articleTitle: A Quadratic Boost Two-Stage Transformerless Inverter for Single Phase Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The compact structure and highly efficient per-formance of the transformer-less inverter (TLI) are gaining popularity for the photovoltaic (PV) application. A decrease in the size of the TLI is possible by removing the bulky /heavy transformer from the conventional PV inverter system. It results in a loss of isolation, and a direct connection between PV and the grid is established through inverters. The direct connection causes the variation of common mode voltage (CMV) during the inverter operation, which further leads to the leakage current. This paper presents a two-stage TLI configuration for five-level output voltage. The front end uses two inductors and two capacitors to provide quadratic boost output to an inverter for multilevel output voltage. A common ground configuration (CGC) helps to mitigate leakage current. Level-shifted pulse width modulation (LS- PWM) is used to accomplish inverter control. Further, the voltage and current stress of the inverter are analyzed for each switch for selecting the power components. The TLI is verified in both MATLAB/Simulink environment and experimentally in the laboratory.

articleTitle: A New Single-Phase Dual-Mode Active Neutral Point-Clamped Five-Level Inverter for Renewable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The paper presents a new single-phase Dual-Mode Active Neutral Point-Clamped Five-Level (ANPC-5L) inverter for Renewable applications. It overcomes the shortcoming of ANPC multilevel converters proposed in the recent literature such as excessive voltage stress on devices, utilization of half the dc-link voltage and the requirement of larger than double the dc-link voltage as compared to the grid peak voltage. Therefore, in this paper, a dual-mode ANPC converter is presented which promises the merits of reduced device stress over a wide range of dc input voltages for grid connected operation. The proposed topology is designed with standard T-type modules using 10 power devices and four dc-links and has the features of bidirectional power flow with an integrated flying capacitor (FC) technique. Moreover, it can be operated in two distinct modes such as boost mode and buck mode for a wide range of the input voltage. Simple level-shifted/phase-shifted pulse width modulation scheme is used for both the boost and a buck mode operation to realize the five-level output voltage waveform. A simple proportional-resonant (PR) controller is developed to study the dynamic response of the system under input voltage and their modes of operation using MATLAB/PLECS software and their results are presented. Finally, a detailed comparison is made with the recent ANPC-5L inverter topologies to highlight the merits of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Shunt Active Power Filter for Power Quality Improvements with PV Array
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this paper a shunt active filter with Solar Photo Voltaic (SPV) panel is controlled using Fuzzy Logic Controller circuit (FLC), also power for Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) is obtained from SPV system through a Sepic converter which works in Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) mode. Power quality problems including harmonic distortion and reactive power consumption have increased as a result of the expanding usage of non-linear loads in electrical power networks Instanta-neous Reactive Power Theory (IRPT) is employed and reference current is generated. Fuzzy logic controller (FLC) is used to provide the compensating current reference of shunt active filter. The DC-link of the shunt APF is continually maintained by the SPV system for long-term harmonic reduction It is validated using MATLAB-Simulink and the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) was maintained within the permissible standards.

articleTitle: A Novel Reduced Based Switch Voltage Tripler Circuit for Electric Fence Energizer Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: High-frequency unipolar High Voltage (HV) pulses find diverse applications, serving as a vigilant shield for safe-guarding a range of sites from buildings and livestock enclosures to vast agricultural expanses and international borders. Developing a Power Energizer circuit (PEC) holds great importance for a wide range of protective applications. This is powered by solar PV that is connected to a DC-DC boost converter, also has a battery backup that is connected to a bi-directional DC-DC boost converter. The performance of the PEC is proposed under various solar irradiance conditions and also under the safe limits of the energizer provided by IEC 60335-2-76:2002 standard [1]. The key feature distinguishing the PEC is its capability to generate HVP, exceeding 15 kV in magnitude, sustained for a microsecond. This is achieved while maintaining a continuous supply of nearly 48 volts for the input DC source, with the discharged pulse conforming to power energizer standards, yielding an energy level of approximately 5 joules.

articleTitle: Development of Software and Hardware for Identification of Interturn Short Circuit in Single-Phase Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The methods of diagnostics of interturn short circuits in transformer and the method of their classification by means of convolutional neural networks are considered. Appli cation of this technology will allow to analyse information in real time mode, classify various deviations and defects.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Microgrid with EV Charging Station, Load Shifting, and DSTATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This work presents an optimization approach for optimal operation of a grid connected microgrid (MG) considering EV charging station, renewable-based generators, DSTATCOM, load shifting, and both active and reactive power loads. DSTATCOM is used to supply the reactive power loads locally instead of purchasing it from the grid. Load shifting strategy is used to reduce dependency on the grid during high electricity pricing hours. The minimization of total annual operating cost of MG is considered as the objective function which includes cost of buying/selling active power from/to the grid, costs related to PV, wind power generator, and DSTATCOM, cost of reactive power purchase from the grid, and operating cost of EV charging station. EV charging station load profile is generated using fuzzy-based approach considering number ofEVs, SOC levels of EVs, and arrival time of EV s to the charging station. The proposed optimization problem is solved using CPLEX solver of GAMS. The simulation results show that the uses of load shifting and DSTACOM facilities significantly reduce the total annual operating cost of MG.

articleTitle: A Novel AMB Laser Welding of Copper Eyelets onto Aluminum Busbars
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The necessity of bonding copper and aluminum in certain Electric vehicle battery pack applications arises from the advantageous properties they each offer: copper excels in conductivity and response, while aluminum contributes to weight reduction. In many instances, the bonding of aluminum and copper can be accomplished through methods such as adhesive bonding, mechanical fastening, fusion welding, and solid-phase welding. Laser welding, renowned for its capacity to join aluminum to a variety of metals, is now receiving serious consideration. This study focuses on achieving a robust connection between two dissimilar metals: pre-strained aluminum and commercially pure copper. Commercial pure aluminum is intentionally strained to narrow the strength gap between the two materials, and the impact of pre-strain on Laser welding is examined. To facilitate a strong joint, nickel plating is added over the pure copper eyelet. This paper presents comparative analysis of both Bolting and AMB laser welding technology in battery pack. Proposed AMB laser welding is cost effective with more reliability and benefits as compared to manual bolting type.

articleTitle: Novel Control Topology for Electric Fence Energizer Based on Small Wind Turbine & Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper introduce a simple electric fence energizer modelling in MATLAB, currently most research is lined with the modelling, simulation, and its implementation using a conventional method i.e., by employing a battery backup system or online power system, but no one has so far established the use of renewable energy and battery back up as a simultaneous source of power for the operation of the electric fence energizer, by using electric energy harvested through small wind turbine, it is show that how battery can charged and simultaneously provide power to the electric fence energizer. The design and topology for the Control circuit at the interference of battery connection, small wind turbine - power transfer topology is being carried out. Standards for electric fence energizer & high voltage pulse application areas are being discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multi Area Load Frequency Control under Bilateral Market Incorporating Renewable Energy Source
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Over the last decade, deregulation has resulted in numerous variations in the power industry. One of the main goals of reformation is to promote privatization. This has resulted in numerous independent power producers to collaborate while employing renewable energy sources. The reformed structure introduces market where power transactions are performed. Under bilateral market, the power is traded between the buyers and sellers based on the agreement. Each generating unit schedules or re-schedules its generation to fulfil the contracted or violated power respectively, with the help of load frequency control. This paper analyses the performance of load frequency control of a thermal and solar thermal integrated two area power system operating under bilateral market. The performance analysis is done using the transfer function model of multi area deregulated power system. The load frequency control is operated under tie line bias control technique. The generating units and transmission line powers are analyzed during contract and violation. Various case studies that include participation of single and multiple generating units to compensate for the contract violation are conducted. The effective performance of load frequency control in a hybrid source bilateral model is validated through case studies.

articleTitle: A Transformer Less Two-Stage Three-Port Power Converter with Battery Storage for PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this paper a transformer less two-stage threeport power converter (TTTPC) with battery storage for photo voltaic (PV) systems is proposed. To address the intermittence of the PV source and to supply uninterrupted power to the load an additional battery storage unit is integrated to the proposed system with a novel front-end three-port converter. The control pulses to the converter are generated based on the decision from mode selector namely: PV to battery (Sepic converter), PV to DC bus (boost converter), PV to both battery and DC bus (Buck and boost converter, respectively), and battery to DC bus (Zeta converter). Further, a six switch five-level inverter is integrated to drive the AC loads at reduced leakage current, lower harmonic distortion and higher efficiency. Performance of the TTTPC under different modes of operation is carried out by using Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Five-Phase System for Various Bus-Clamping Space Vector Based Pulse Width Modulation Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The area of multiple phase systems has substantially grown as they have the greatest power density. To operate these systems effectively, requires different modulation techniques in various loading conditions. This paper deals with five-phase voltage source inverter and their modulation techniques in space vector based approach. By utilizing small, medium, and large space vectors, various pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques can be applied, including the conventional space vector PWM (CSVPWM), the discontinuous PWM and bus-clamping PWM (BCPWM). This BCPWM results in lower harmonic distortion than CSVPWM and this trend is same in case of switching energy loss. But switching energy loss in BCPWM is a strong function of power factor. The proposed technique is simulated and results are analyzed.

articleTitle: A New Single-Phase Fault-Tolerant T-Type Five-Level Inverter with 100% DC Utilization
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The paper presents a new single-phase fault-tolerant five-level inverter with 100% DC utilization. Self-balancing of dc capacitors with reduced device counts and compact T-type structure will enhance the overall reliability of the proposed topology. A simple half-bridge circuit with two additional semiconductor devices were added to the topology to obtain more redundant states which can support the five-level generation under most of the fault conditions. Moreover, the waveform quality and the power handling capability is ensured under various open/short circuit fault conditions of the proposed topology with the help of redundant switches and modified pulse width modulation scheme. Further, reduced device count and minimum number of conducing devices in each cycle ensure the highest efficiency with its counter parts. The proposed circuit is tested through MATLAB/Simulink environment for various open circuit fault conditions and the results are presented. Finally, a comprehensive comparison is made to highlight the merits of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Trash Classification System for Lakes and Water Bodies Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The growing accumulation of rubbish in lakes and bodies of water poses a huge environmental concern that necessitates creative solutions. To address this issue, the study proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) powered trash classification system based on transfer learning. This system seeks to revolutionize waste management in lakes and water bodies by leveraging AI and machine learning (ML) technology. The methodology integrates computer vision, advanced ML algorithms, and robotics to identify, classify, and collect various sorts of trash in bodies of water. The system incorporates a pre-trained residual network (ResN et-50) model. Extensive simulations are carried out, and the experiments show that transfer learning using ResN et50 can obtain great results in classifying garbage photos into numerous categories. With an accuracy of 95.6%, the model offers a promising deep-learning option for automated waste management systems. The model's strong precision and recall scores demonstrate its ability to classify various waste types in real-world contexts correctly.

articleTitle: Fuzzy C-Means Clustering Approach for Green IoT in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Cluster-based routing or Hierarchical is a widely recognized approach with particular benefits in terms of scalability and communication efficiency. In Wireless Sensor Networks supported <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$IoT$</tex>, the utilization of clustered routing is a cost-effective method of data collection and transmission, where nodes with the most energy remaining can be utilized to collect and transmit data. This paper proposed a soft Fuzzy C-Means Dynamic Clustering (FCM-DC) Approach. A new Cluster Head (CH) selection technique was presented also. The proposed model was compared with an existing cluster based routing protocol, LEACH protocol, and LEACH-C protocol. The proposed FCM-DC model reduce the packet delay about 16% in 50 nodes scenario and 86% in 100 nodes scenario compared with LEACH.

articleTitle: SOH Based Power Sharing Algorithm for Second-life Batteries Using Health Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The uncertain capacity differences in second-life batteries due to internal characteristics require SOH balancing for SLB modules. The most popular SOC balancing does not guarantee the SOH balance and battery efficiency. Many works of literature try to extract the SOH parameter through either the number of cycles or DOD change. Still, current rate and temperature also have significant influence over the SOH parameter. To solve this problem, in this article the SOH is derived from the most effective health degradation parameters based on DOD and charge rate. An online SOH estimation method is proposed, and according to the determined SOHs, a power-sharing control algorithm is developed to realize the SOH balancing. This article employs the conventional battery energy storage system (BESS) as the second-life battery module since most EVs utilize the bi-directional DC-DC converter boost-buck configuration. MATLAB simulation and floating-point DSP controller hardware-in-loop (CHIL) experimentation results are presented for discharging, DC bus voltage variation and change in power demand cases to verify the proposed algorithm. The algorithm performs decent power-sharing according to their SOH values based on DOD and current rates.

articleTitle: Design, Development and Performance of Cryocooler Drive Electronics for Sea Surface Temperature Monitor Payload
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Knowledge of sea surface temperature along with ocean colour information provides a vital information to identify and locate the potential fisheries zone (PFZ). ISRO has developed one Sea Surface Temperature Monitor (SSTM) payload for oceanographic studies. SSTM images in Thermal Infrared (TIR) region and the imaging detector needs to be operated at cryo temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\approx 50\mathrm{K})$</tex> for higher responsivity. To achieve desired performance, detector is integrated in a motor-based cryocooler. This paper presents the details of ISRO's first indigenously developed Drive Electronics for in-orbit TIR cryocooler. Temperature of 50K with stability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45_\text{mK}$</tex> is achieved. Electronics design paves way to development for future cryocooler stability requirement <10mK with higher efficiency.

articleTitle: Power Inverter Performance with Trapezoidal Triangular Carrier and Triangular Based SPWM Technique: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Output voltage quality and efficiency of multilevel inverters vastly depend on the modulation technique employed. However, the performance of high frequency modulation technique depends on the type of carrier signal, modulating, as well as modulation index. Identification of the best modulation strategy it can reduce voltage and current THDs, as well as power losses. This paper presents a comparative analysis between trapezoidal triangular carrier and triangular carrier based SPWM on the performances of a power converter. The study investigates the effects of varying the modulation index and carrier frequency, and identifies optimal points where the trapezoidal triangular carrier signal-based SPWM technique demonstrates superior performance. Additionally, the power losses of this carrier signal have been compared to that of the conventional carrier based SPWM modulation approach. The comprehensive study has been conducted using the MATLAB Simulink software. The simulation findings indicate that though the trapezoidal triangle carrier based SPWM technique exhibits lower voltage total harmonic distortions (THDs) compared to the conventional technique, its produces high current total harmonics distortions for the same resistive inductive load and high inverter losses.

articleTitle: An Ultra High Gain Quadratic Boost Converter with Low Electric Stress and Lower Inductor Currents for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This work presents an ultra-high gain quadratic boost (UHGQB) converter for photovoltaic applications with a detailed operational and steady-state analysis. Further, the comparative analysis of the UHGQB converter with existing converters suggests that the UHGQB converter performs better in terms of total component count, TVS, TCS, SDP rating, volume of inductors and capacitors, and efficiency. In addition, MATLAB-based simulations are conducted for a 650 V, 1 kW, and 50 kHz system. The open and closed loop simulation results validated the satisfactory steady-state and dynamic performance of the UHGQB converter. Furthermore, the efficiency analysis was carried out and the UHGQB converter was found to have the highest efficiency of 95.2 %. Therefore, the proposed UHGQB converter can be adopted for photovoltaic systems as well as other high-voltage applications.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle to Vehicle (V2V) Power Transfer with On-Board Network and Capacitor-Link
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a new configuration and analysis to share energy between electric vehicle to vehicle (V2V). The proposed converter uses on-board equipment of the electric vehicle (EV) and an externally connected capacitor. This configuration is capable of transferring energy between EVs with either identical or non-identical battery ratings. Further, it uses only the DC-DC converter components of the on-board equipment. Thus, reduces the number of devices conduction during the V2V power transfer. The operation of the proposed arrangement is validated by using simulation studies and the results are presented for different battery charging conditions.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of NoSQL and Time Series Databases for Fast Data Acquisition System of Indus-2
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Relational databases have been the go-to data logging solution in the scientific community for years. But due to the rapidly changing nature of scientific instruments and the data generated by them, relational databases have begun to fall short of the requirement. In recent years NoSQL and time series databases have come up. These databases have a flexible data model, have horizontal scalability, and are distributed in nature, which helps them handle large volumes of data. This paper provides a comparative study of performance of Cassandra, MongoDB and InfluxDB databases that are used for logging fast data from the data acquisition system of Synchrotron Radiation Source Indus-2. The study uses both the open source synthetic benchmarks and Indus-2 machine parameter data to ascertain the relative performance of the three databases.

articleTitle: Grid Connected Three Level T-Type Inverter Based APF for Smart Grid Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this study, a three-level T -type multilevel inverter-based DSTATCOM for a grid-connected operations is introduced. This three-level T -type MLI incorporates the benefits of a two-level voltage source inverter, including lower switching component count, lower switching losses, as well as simplified control operations, with the advantages of a three-level inverter, such as lower switching losses and enhanced output voltage waveforms. The d-q reference frame is used to develop a control system for the T -type MLI -based DSTATCOM in grid-connected mode. The maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methodology, performed using perturb and observe method, is efficiently connected with the reference current estimate using the d-q reference frame. This MPPT approach dynamically changes the solar panel's operating point by perturbing its voltage and detecting the consequent change in power output. The algorithm is refined iteratively to optimize its modifications for effective tracking and operating at or near the maximum power point, regardless of changing conditions. The Perturb and Observe (P&O) approach combined with a d-q reference frame increases DSTATCOM performance by allowing it to adjust for harmonic currents and inject active power into the grid. The MATLAB/Simulink framework was used to simulate aT-type Multilevel Inverter (MLI) in a grid-connected DSTATCOM, demonstrating its effectiveness in eliminating for harmonic currents and delivering power to a grid.

articleTitle: Broadband Absorption Spectroscopy for Carbon Dioxide Gas Sensing Using Hollow Core Fibre
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Carbon dioxide gas impacts environment and human beings. However, the accurate prediction of molecular level is a challenging task. We presented an optical sensing approach for identification of carbon dioxide in a gas mixture by broadband absorption spectroscopy for understanding the concentration level of this molecule in the specific region. The use of optical sensing technique for CO2 offers several improvements in terms of selectivity, sensitivity, response time, and detection. A broadband supercontinuum laser source (spectral range from 800 nm to 2500 nm) is used to measure carbon dioxide's absorption characteristics in the 2017 nm region. A hollow core waveguide with an optical path length of 10m and an FTIR spectrometer was used to visualize the spectra. The least detection limit was calculated as 64.658 ppm at 1o for a data acquisition speed of 20 s.

articleTitle: Day Ahead Load Demand Forecasting based on LSTM Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: load demand Forecasting is a crucial part in modern energy management systems, grid operators in resource allocation and maintaining grid stability. This research paper introduces an innovative methodology for load demand forecasting employing Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks, a specific type of recurrent neural network (RNN) adepted by capturing long-term dependencies within sequential data. This work proposed a LSTM-based load forecasting model that utilizes one year of historical electricity consumption data from the Chhattisgarh state of India. The model is designed to predict day ahead load demand for the subsequent year. As the energy sector advances towards a smarter and more sustainable future, the integration of sophisticated LSTM based forecasting techniques holds significant promise. The technique facilitates the optimization of energy distribution, encourage the seamless integration of renewable energy sources, and the resilience of power grids. The model performance analysis is presented by utilizing Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values as the evaluation metric.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Controller Design for Percutaneous Interventional Procedures
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The aim of this research work is to implement a trajectory tracking controller for a flexible needle within a tissue region, using a neural network-based approach. Initially, a kinematic model for steerable needle inside the tissue domain is considered based on a unicycle model while considering nonholonomic constraints. Subsequently, a neural network (NN) architecture based closed loop control strategy is implemented to track a desired trajectory on a specified plane. The efficacy of the developed controller is confirmed through simulation studies. Furthermore, a comparative study is conducted, involving a standard Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller, to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed controller. The simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed control scheme outperforms the conventional PID approach.

articleTitle: A Stealth False Data Attack on State Estimation with Minimal Network Information
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Power system state estimation(SE) is more prone to cyber-attacks being a key operation mechanism to maintain the system observability. To strengthen the cyber security of SE and develop efficient attack detection techniques it is required to examine the existing residual based bad data detection(BDD) security mechanism by developing new, intelligent and stealth false data attack(FDA) models which is near practical. To this aim, the presented work focuses on model free deep convolutional generative adversarial networks(DCGAN) based single bus target stealth FDA injection on SE with minimal network information. Against the previous model based methods in this the inherent measurement data distribution and physical model is learnt only by means of the easily available measurement data on the single bus target area. The single bus target area method is the near practical approach and will be difficult to recognize as against the previous tie-line based and whole area attack region. The generated attack is validated on IEEE 14 bus system and the experimental results shows that it exhibits sufficiently high intensity and residual within the predefined threshold as for the normal data and can easily bypass the BDD mechanism with high success rate.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Lead Free CH3NH3SnI3 Perovskite Solar Cell: A Simulation Approach by SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The toxicity issue is a major obstacle to the broad commercialization of Lead (Pd)-based Perovskite Solar Cells (PSCs). In such scenarios, Tin (Sn)-based PSC can be crucial to the widespread adoption of high-performance SC. In this study, a Sn-based structure of FTO/Ti0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Spiro-OMeTADI Au has been proposed. A sequential strategy is adopted to evaluate the energy level, recombination rate, the bandgap of the absorber, work function, reflective coating, temperature, typical J - V and Q- E curve of the structure using SCAPS ID software. The optimized structure attained maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.95 %, with open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>) of 0.9622 V, short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 33.87 ma/cm2 and fill factor (FF) of 82.69% at 300k. The outcomes of this numerical simulation can offer an insightful approach for fabricating viable, economical and highly efficient Sn-based PSC.

articleTitle: Hybrid Carrier Frequency Based Modulation Strategy to Improve Efficiency of Voltage Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Rapid advancement of high-speed power switching devices lead to widespread usage of Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) in variable speed drive systems. The quality of the power delivered by a VSI is highly dependent on the modulation strategy. Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) is the traditional modulation strategy for VSIs. PWMs are generated mostly based on fixed frequency carrier waveform. These classical modulation strategies suffer from the high total harmonic distortion in low carrier frequency (CF) and high-power loss in high CF. To diminish the THD (Total Harmonic Distortion) and power loss of the VSI, this paper proposes a hybrid carrier frequency (HCF) method. The performance of the proposed method has been tested on an experimental setup for a validation and the results are compared with the classical approach. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach increases the efficiency by reducing the switching losses without increasing the complexity of the PWM.

articleTitle: Supraharmonic Analysis by Welch's-Power Spectral Density Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Supraharmonic analysis, as applied to power systems through Welch's Power Spectral Density Estimation, emerges as a crucial technique for assessing the stability and reliability of electrical grids. This paper offers a novel approach to investigate the non-standard frequency components and disturbances that can affect power distribution networks. By breaking down the electrical signals into supraharmonic components, this method enables a deep understanding of complex power system behaviors and the sources of instability. Welch's Power Spectral Density Estimation plays a pivotal role in this process, allowing for a detailed examination of the spectral content of power system signals. The extraction of supraharmonic information facilitates the identification of irregularities and anomalies, which are often elusive when analyzing traditional harmonic frequencies. The use of various window functions enhances the precision of Supraharmonic Analysis, allowing for a finely tuned investigation of power system behaviors and disturbances. Different window functions offer flexibility in capturing specific characteristics within the signals, making it easier to identify and isolate irregularities and anomalies. Among triangular,hanning, and hamming windows, reduced spectral leakage and smoother power spectral density are achieved from the hamming window. Also, the comparative analysis of harmonics and supraharmonics by Welch's Power Spectral Density estimation has been performed.

articleTitle: Optimal Droop Control for Current Sharing among Different Types of Battery Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This article discusses droop control schemes for various types of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The SOC-based droop control scheme, aims to maintain equal State of Charge (SOC) among multiple BESSs. However, this approach results in different incremental costs for different battery types. To minimize the total battery degradation cost, IC-based droop control scheme is discussed. This scheme distributes the current among different types of batteries in such a way that they operate at the same incremental cost. The effectiveness of discussed con-trol schemes was evaluated through simulation studies using a test system with different types of BESS and varying load conditions. The DC bus voltage was kept constant using secondary control. This research provides useful insights into the optimal control of BESS to reduce the total degradation cost.

articleTitle: Detection of DC Faults in Ring-Main DC Microgrid System Using Naïve Bayes Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: DC Microgrids have emerged as a compelling solution for boosting energy efficiency, integrating renewable energy sources and strengthening grid resilience. The limited adoption of DC microgrid is partially ascribed to the complexities involved in devising a trustworthy protection system. The challenges are attributed to absence of natural zero crossing in fault current, presence of different converters, power variation of DERs due to weather intermittency. Failure to address the above-mentioned concerns lead to decreased grid resilience, potentially due to relay breakdown in high stress situations. In this context, a Naïve Bayes-based protection scheme has been proposed for DC microgrid for varying network and weather conditions. The proposed fault detection methods offer robust and adaptable means to detect faults in the DC microgrid system. With accurate and robust protection under varying fault scenarios the proposed scheme provides a platform for the wider acceptance of DC microgrid.

articleTitle: Current Control of Sensorless BLDC Motor Using Hysteresis Control
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The superior performance and operational benefits of brushless DC (BLDC) motors have increased their adoption in several industries. As BLDC technology continues to progress, its impact on various industries is expected to grow. Brushless motors with and without sensors offer precise control and smooth operation at low speeds. Even though motors with sensors provide higher speeds and more cost-effective operation, more power can be extracted from sensorless motors. Sensorless BLDC motors depend on estimation techniques to calculate rotor position, which means that estimation accuracy is crucial for their performance. For that, a new approach for determining commutation instants is presented in this work, which is the Volt/Hz method. By comparing line-to-line voltages and their differences, unit templates are generated. Hysteresis controllers are used to provide precise adjustments and efficient performance for BLDC motors, which minimizes error. This technique, which does not rely on back-EMF zero-crossings, offers a distinctive viewpoint. To achieve the Volt/Hz method, the switching pulses are generated by using the hysteresis controller. To fully study and confirm how well this BLDC drive works with the new methodology, simulations are done in the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment.

Author Keywords: ZCP (Zero Crossing Points) and Speed Estimation

articleTitle: Investigation of Core Loss in Electric Vehicle Induction Motor Using Finite Element Analysis for Performance Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Temperature rise in a 3ϕ, Totally Enclosed Fan Cooled (TEFC)., Squirrel Cage Induction Motor (SCIM) used in Electric Vehicles (EV) is effected by core loss. The temperature rise is a function of core loss and other losses. Since, the core loss components eddy current and hysteresis losses are a function of flux and flux density, Finite Element Method (FEM) is used to obtain average maximum flux density at different loads. Core loss is varying with respect to load and hence temperature rise, resistance value, starting torque to maximum torque <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\displaystyle \frac{T_{st}}{T_{\max}})$</tex> ratio and current drawn at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\displaystyle \frac{T_{st}}{T_{\max}})$</tex> also varies which is so far assumed constant in reality. The analysis is made on the effect of core loss on SCIM used in EV for performance enhancement. The results reveals that when the variable core loss is considered, temperature rise is reduced and the SCIM rating is enhanced for 20%.

articleTitle: Common Mode Voltage Reduction in Space Vector Modulated Direct Torque Controlled Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)

authors.preferredName: S V S Phani Kumar Ch

abstract: Common mode voltage (CMV) can have detrimental effects on the performance of induction motor drive. The common-mode voltage causes leakage current to flow causing consequently unwanted tripping of switchgears, premature failure of bearings etc. This paper is focused on the mitigation of the resulting CMV and hence common mode current by reducing the number of transitions in common mode voltage. For this the three-phase two level h-9 inverter topology is presented in this paper. The proposed topology takes advantage of device junction capacitance (DJC) effect, occurring across switches in the OFF state, to achieve neutral point clamping. Further proposed topology is implemented on SVM-DTC and results are verified with simulation results.

articleTitle: Control and Implementation of Interleaved DC-DC Converter-Based IPMSM Drive for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper discusses controlling and implementing an interleaved DC-DC converter-based Interior permanent mag-net synchronous motor (IPMSM) drive for electric vehicle (EV) applications. The choice of an IPMSM motor stems from its supe-rior efficiency and power-density characteristics. Field-Oriented Control (FOC) is employed for control purposes, providing independent control over the magnetizing and torque-producing components of the motor. Including an interleaved bidirectional DC-DC converter (IBC) within the IPMSM drive circuit enhances overall system performance and boosts battery voltage. Average current mode control (ACMC) is employed for IBC. Additionally, the interleaved converter promotes current sharing, reducing the size and weight of inductors while contributing to ripple reduction and enhanced system reliability. In this control scheme, the speed reference aligns with the Indian drive cycle (IDC), and the load profile is based on the dynamic model of an EV. The entire closed-loop system is simulated using MATLAB. Furthermore, the study observes the motoring and regenerative operations of the IPMSM employing the IDC.

articleTitle: An Image Retrieval System Based on Textual Information and Features
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In today's world as there is a rapid growth of digitalization, searching and retrieving of relevant images from large datasets efficiently and accurately is challenging. There are two Image Retrieval Methods. These are Text-Based Image Retrieval and Content-Based Image Retrieval. In this manuscript, we are going to implement both of these methods together to retrieve similar restaurant images of the same name and belonging to either the same franchise or having the same features as the query image. CBIR can be used to identify images of similar color and features from dataset to given query image and OCR is used to identify the textual information present on images. For more accurate results we are adding a phonetic-based Fuzzy string matching algorithm to improve the efficiency of OCR as the names of restaurants may not always be in a formal style.

Author Keywords: Phonetic based Fuzzy string matching Algorithm

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of EV Charger Using AI Based Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The rapidly growing demand of electric vehicle(EV) has a detrimental impact on power quality of the utility distribution grid. The choice of EV battery charger design is crucial in reducing power quality issues. Conventional diode bridge rectifier(DBR) based converters introduce significant harmonics which also adversely affects the battery life. A DBR interfaced with a zeta converter can reduce the power supply distortions and improve the input power factor during battery charging. PI controllers are comprehensively applied in battery chargers; nevertheless, their performance tends to suffer under system dynamics. The diversity of electric vehicles (EVs) and the dynamic changes in battery operating conditions introduce numerous uncertainties, making an artificial intelligence (AI) based controller a preferable choice for EV charging applications. The performance of an isolated zeta converter with PI, fuzzy logic and Artificial Neural Network(ANN) based controllers is tested in MATLAB/Simulink environment under different operating conditions. Analysis of the results clearly indicates that AI based controllers are not only effective in reducing harmonics but also in ensuring improved performance under both steady-state and dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Direct Torque Control and Model Predictive Control Based on Voltage Vector Strategy for SRM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The power-torque characteristics of the magnetless switched reluctance motor (SRM) are well-suited for electric vehicle traction motor applications. However, the SRM faces a significant challenge in the form of high torque ripple, attributed to the improper selection of turn-on and turn-off switching states. Additionally, commutation torque ripple can contribute to overall torque fluctuations. To address these issues, this paper introduces a finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) for SRM drives. This control strategy aims to minimize torque and flux ripple, providing improved performance in both steady and dynamic states. In comparison to classical direct torque control (DTC) and model predictive control (MPC) techniques, the proposed methods exhibit reduced torque and flux ripples. The efficacy of the FCS-MPC with a single prediction horizon is validated through simulations in MATLAB/Simulink, considering both static and dynamic behaviors. The simulations enable an in-depth analysis of flux ripple and torque ripple, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: V2V Charging and Solar Integration to Overcome Range Anxiety in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) grapples with a significant challenge known as ‘range anxiety’, which is the fear of depleting the battery charge before reaching the destination. This paper proposes an inventive strategy to mitigate range anxiety by integrating Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) charging as a fundamental component of the EV ecosystem. The V2V charging mechanism harnesses the energy-sharing capabilities of EVs, facilitating power exchange between vehicles on the road. Our research targets the integration of solar panels onto the source vehicle, serving as a renewable energy source for V2V charging. The discussion commences by addressing the current state of range anxiety and the constraints of traditional EV charging infrastructure. The paper elucidates the design and implementation of a solar panel system on the source vehicle, emphasizing its efficiency and energy generation potential. To validate our claims, simulation results conducted in the MATLAB/Simulink environment are presented, offering a comprehensive analysis of the proposed V2V charging system's effectiveness. This paper significantly contributes to the growing body of knowledge surrounding innovative solutions for the EV industry. It underscores the potential of V2V charging, in tandem with solar panels, as a promising stride towards a more sustainable and range-anxiety-free future for electric vehicle users. The primary targets of this paper encompass elucidating V2V charging, detailing solar integration, conducting simulations, and analyzing results to provide valuable insights for the advancement of electric vehicle technology.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Strategy for Asymmetrical Half-Bridge Converter in Switched Reluctance Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A novel fault-tolerant method for handling switch faults in the Asymmetrical Half- Bridge Converter (ABC) used in Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) Drives is presented in this paper. Many power switch failures are handled using the suggested technique. The d-q trajectory approach is used in conjunction with a single current sensor scheme to diagnose defects in the switches. MATLAB 2022a simulations with an 8/6 four-phase (SRM) drive are used to verify the method's efficacy. Hysteresis current controllers and advanced angle commutation control techniques are the control strategies used in the simulations. The suggested approach guarantees that the system dynamics won't be impacted in the event of a short circuit or open circuit failure in any switch of the converter.

articleTitle: Soft Switching Dual Active Bridge Converter for Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure on Dual Load Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper introduces a modified Dual Active Bridge (DAB) topology combined with an LLC resonant converter for bidirectional power transfer and multiple output voltage capabilities, focusing on its application within Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. This converter, featuring a two-stage power conversion system, offers significant advantages of high-power applications, including high efficiency, reduced voltage stress, cost-effectiveness, and the distinct Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) property, setting it apart from isolated and non-isolated DC-DC converters. The paper delves into a detailed analysis of the converter, elucidating its operational principles, soft-switching behaviour, steady-state characteristics, output attributes, and control mechanisms. A simulation involving a dual active proposed topology with a power rating of 50 kilowatts has been conducted utilizing the MATLAB/Simulink software platform, and the resultant findings have been duly observed and documented.

articleTitle: Unitized Double Sided Linear Switched Reluctance Motor with Auxiliary Winding for Rope Less Elevators
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper analyze the Double Sided Linear Switched Reluctance Motor (DSLS-RM) with auxiliary winding for rope less elevators. Linear switched reluctance motor are two types based on the structure, single sided and double sided linear switched reluctance motor. Power electronic devices achieve the modulation of the speed and force developed in the linear motors. Instead, an auxiliary winding can used and modulation of force and speed can be achieved in the double sided linear switched reluctance motor. By using an auxiliary winding in double sided linear switched reluctance motor the flux weakening and strengthening will occurs in the stator, due to which the modulation of force and speed is possible without any power electronic devices. Due to addition of auxiliary winding in the stator the four modes of operation is possible by changing the direction of excitation of the windings. The modulation of force and speed for the DSLS-RM is analyzed using FEA analysis tool (ANSYS Maxwell). The experimental model of the double sided linear switched reluctance motor has been set up, analyzed and compared with simulation results.

Author Keywords: Double Sided Linear Switched Reluctance Motor (DSLS-RM)

articleTitle: Protection Coordination Impact on Reliability of Distribution Systems With Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The effectiveness and reliability of a power distribution system hinge on the establishment and maintenance of efficient coordination between protective relays. Alongside the prevention of unwarranted overloads, inadequate coordination among relays may lead to an increased likelihood of revealing concealed failures within crucial components of the protection system, like Circuit Breakers. To assess the potential degradation of system reliability due to protection system malfunctions, this study proposes the utilization of a Markov model (MM) in combination with a Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) algorithm. Furthermore, the study also addresses the impact of the protective equipment mis-coordination on the concealed failure of protection systems. Subsequently, using a modified Canadian benchmark distribution system, the study computes the reliability indices of System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) and Expected Energy Not Supplied (EENS) for three distinct scenarios characterized by varying relay settings and protection coordination. The findings are subsequently presented to demonstrate how miscoordination of protection systems within the distribution network can affect the overall system reliability.

articleTitle: Efficient Contaminant Identification in sEMG Signals using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) signal classification applications, such as upper limb prosthesis, have increased in recent years. Eliminating unwanted noise signal for the exact and controlled motion of prosthesis is imperative. Noise in signal make a model biased and lead to mis-classifications. During the usage of a prosthetic arm, mis-classifications of hand gestures can cause it to behave erratically. The choice of a proper filter depends on the type of noise. Therefore, it is necessary to correctly identify the noise and filter it without increasing its hardware complexity. In this article, a study on three approaches to identify four commonly occurring noise in sEMG signal is performed, which is useful for filter selection. The three approaches include the tabular feature, sequence feature, and image feature based classification. Six different classifiers are used to compare the three approaches on the basis of accuracy, time consumption, and memory consumption. Models are also tested on varying noise levels for robustness analysis. On all the levels of noise, the sequence feature based classification approach gives a reasonably good accuracy while consuming the least time and memory.

articleTitle: Design of a User Friendly IOT Based Interface for the Collection of Multimodal Data from Autistic Children
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition marked by challenges in social communication and the presence of restricted interests and repetitive behaviors. Early diagnosis is crucial for providing necessary support to children with ASD. This paper discusses the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in expediting and enhancing the accuracy of ASD diagnosis. Unlike a single definitive test, diagnosis involves a multidisciplinary approach considering developmental history, behavior, and social interaction skills. AI algorithms offer a promising solution by analyzing diverse data sources, such as medical records and genetic information, to identify patterns associated with ASD. The combined analysis of questionnaire responses and video data allows doctor to predict the diagnosis of ASD. The application serves as a preliminary screening tool, encouraging parents to seek further evaluation from healthcare professionals. To address this issue, this paper proposes an application which holds the potential to make ASD diagnosis more accurate, efficient, and accessible, ultimately contributing to improved outcomes for children with ASD.

articleTitle: Long-Term Load Forecasting: A Systematic Review with Focus on Microgrid Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The long-term load forecasting (LTLF) plays an important role in multiple areas of power distribution system including demand side management and system planning. The LTLF models can be helpful for utility in providing valuable inputs to support grid expansion and electricity purchase agreements. Therefore, the research in the field of load forecasting is ongoing and evolving continuously. This paper presents a systematic review of different approaches that have been reported recently in the literature for LTLF of distribution grid and microgrids. The critical review and comparison among the LTLF models have been carried out based on multiple aspects such as methodology, objective, applicability, forecasting accuracy and error matrix, forecasting horizon and historical data requirements with unique outlook on industry-based acceptability challenges and operational complexities. Many conventional models described in the literature and also being used by the utilities are old and were developed with low resolution data. This paper also highlights the area of improvements in the existing LTLF model as with the current widespread availability of high-resolution data from sensors and smart meters. This review also focusses on the problem addressed by the existing literatures, results obtained by the forecasting models and methods to examine and validate the results. Further, the review work has also been extended to examine the feasibility of real-time deployment of the forecasting models mentioned in the literature. By this approach and comparison of different LTLF models, a few algorithms are highlighted which provide better and improved performance and have the potential of deployment in the distribution level microgrids.

articleTitle: Cost-Efficient Smart Home Security System Based On NodeMCU And Arduino with IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: An efficient and reliable security system is always an important requirement for residential buildings. Though there are already some options available in the commercial home security segment, the budget constraint always plays a vital role for the general customers. In this paper, a customizable and scalable home security system has been developed based on NodeMCU and Arduino, keeping in mind the price constraint. The Internet of Things (IoT), which is an important modern technology, has also been incorporated in this system to make the system smart, reliable and fast. NodeMCU and Arduino UNO are programmable according to the need. Smoke detector, ultrasonic sensor and LDR sensor have been incorporated for taking inputs from the real world environment. The use of IoT makes it possible for the user to access the sensor data in real time from anywhere in the world. In addition to that, an alert system has been developed, which analyzes the information and alerts the user even at a far distance in the real time.

articleTitle: Design, Modelling and Seamless Control of an Offgrid DFIG-Battery Energy Storage Based Wind Energy Conversion System for Remote Dwellings
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This research work presents modelling, design and control of an off-grid doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) and battery energy storage (BES) based wind energy conversion system for remote dwellings. Variability in generated power by the wind energy conversion system (WECS) makes it a challenge for microgrid operators to fulfill the power demand of connected local loads. Therefore, integration of BES along with power generated by DFIG together meets local demand. Any sudden fluctuations in generated power by WECS is absorbed by BES and it also stores excess generation of WECS for meeting demand in situations when WECS generation is low and load demand is relatively high. Moreover, system has capability to isolate DFIG stator at low/ very high wind speed conditions and feeds local loads using BES. As wind speed is reinstated within optimal speed range for power generation, system is connected to DFIG stator, which then feeds generated wind power to local loads. Complete design of wind turbine, DFIG and control of converters for this application is demonstrated in this research work and performance of proposed system is validated using developed model in Matlab Simulink R2017b software.

articleTitle: Optimum Tuning of 1&2-dof TID-F Controllers for a MAGLEV System with Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this work, a rigorous comparative study is carried out between the 1-dof tilt-integral-derivative controller with filter (1-dof TID-F) and the 2-dof tilt-integral-derivative controller with filter (2-dof TID-F) for simultaneous stabilization and precise position control of a laboratory scale magnetic levitation system (MAGLEV). TID controller is basically a modification of the traditional PID controller in which the proportional gain is swapped out for a non-integer order tilting term. Again, in series with the derivative term, a fractional order (FO) filter is introduced to reshape the frequency response curve because FO system has tremendous potential in modelling and control of inner dynamics of highly non-linear and unstable physical system like MAGLEV. For designing and tuning of 1&2-dof TID-F controller parameters a modern soft computing based nature inspired optimization algorithm, popularly known as, Moth Flame Optimization is deployed. Various simulation and real-time results demonstrate that the proposed 2-dof TID- F controller improves time and frequency domain performance metrics while also providing superior reference input tracking ability.

articleTitle: Intelligent Maintenance Scheduling and Decision Support Model for Industry 4.0 System Based on Severity Factors and Priority Weights
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) plays a crucial role in ensuring the reliability and efficiency of industrial system and its components. However, existing research often overlooks the critical consideration of uncertainty and variability in scheduling maintenance tasks, leading to sub-optimal decisions. Efficiently planning maintenance tasks is paramount, and this paper ad-dresses these challenges by introducing an algorithm based on several factors. These severity factors are degradation rate, remaining useful life (RUL), criticality, and failure consequences, each contributing to the overall priority of maintenance tasks. This paper presents a comprehensive approach i.e. Intelligent Maintenance Scheduling and Decision Support (IMS&DS) model for predictive maintenance scheduling in industry 4.0. Moreover, it also considers how resources are assigned and the time needed for repair to avoid doing maintenance tasks too early and to handle uncertainties. The proposed method ensures that maintenance schedules are optimized to minimize the risk of component failure while efficiently utilizing available resources. It also demonstrates the applicability of the proposed algorithm through case studies and severity analysis. This complete framework can be used to enhance maintenance planning and can be readily adopted for any field, revolutionizing the asset management paradigm.

articleTitle: A Metaheuristic Approach Based Adaptive Filter Design for EEG Noise Mitigation Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Electroencephalography stands as a well-established clinical procedure, pivotal in diagnosing a myriad of brain disorders. However, electroencephalogram (EEG) waveforms are susceptible to an array of noise sources, which significantly complicate EEG data analysis. In this study, the authors have employed adaptive filtering in conjunction with metaheuristic algorithms to mitigate noise in EEG signals. Specifically, we have utilized the Harmony Search (HS), Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA), and Preacher's Optimization Algorithm (POA) to address artifacts within epileptic EEG signals. We have quantified various fidelity parameters, including Mean Squared Error (MSE), Maximum Error (ME), and the output Signal-to-Noise Ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(SNR_{o})$</tex>. Notably, our proposed adaptive filter based on POA has demonstrated superior performance when compared to previously documented filtering techniques. In summary, our proposed approach exhibits enhanced accuracy and is deemed more suitable for EEG filtering when contrasted with existing methods.

articleTitle: Evaluating Model Performance Through a User-Centric Explainable Framework for Probabilistic Load Forecasting Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Third International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Load forecasting models ensure efficient, secure, and stable operation of the modern power system. Probabilistic forecasting accounts for uncertainties associated with missing features that are often overlooked by deterministic approaches. However, machine learning-based probabilistic models are complicated. This paper proposes a user-centric explainable AI framework that presents global and local interpretations aligned with the expertise and explanation needs of the targeted user. The overall influence of temporal and spatial exogenous features at the model development stage is evaluated using the Permutation Feature Importance technique. Such an explanation provides a holistic picture of the knowledge gained by the Gradient Boosting Regressor-based probabilistic load forecasting model. Further-more, the proposed framework suggests the implementation of SHapely Additive exPlanations (SHAP) at the post-deployment stage for individual forecast instances. Local explanations provided by SHAP are used to distinguish between interval forecasts with higher and lower forecast accuracy. Such distinction is applied for both the lower and upper bounds of the forecast interval. This is specifically useful for the non-AI expert end-users that need load forecasts for their strategizing their daily operations. This work is validated on the Kaggle data set on the national load demand of Panama supported with several other exogenous features such as weather-related quantities, holidays, and date-time details. Results show the efficacy of the proposed framework and its ability to provide user-friendly interpretations aligned with users' explanation goals.

articleTitle: Bregman Divergence Based Approach for Adaptive System Identification and Line Enhancement
